description: In a string composed of 'L', 'R', and 'X' characters, like "RXXLRXRXL", a move consists of either replacing one occurrence of "XL" with "LX", or replacing one occurrence of "RX" with "XR". Given the starting string start and the ending string end, return true if and only if there exists a sequence of moves to transform one string to the other.

examples.explanation: We can transform start to end following valid moves of 'R' rightwards and 'L' leftwards past 'X'.

constraints: Both start and end will only consist of characters in 'L', 'R', and 'X'.

title: Snapshot Array
description: Implement a SnapshotArray that supports the following interface: SnapshotArray(int length) initializes an array-like data structure with the given length; void set(index, val) sets the value at the given index to be equal to val; int snap() takes a snapshot of the array and returns the snap_id; int get(index, snap_id) returns the value at the given index, at the time we took the snapshot with the given snap_id.

examples.explanation: SnapshotArray created with length 3. set(0, 5) modifies index 0. snap() returns snap_id = 0. get(0, 0) returns 5.

constraints: 0 <= snap_id < (the total number of times snap() is called)
At most 5 * 10^4 calls will be made to set, snap, and get.

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
description: Given the root of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid binary search tree (BST). A valid BST is defined as: the left subtree of a node contains only nodes with keys strictly less than the node's key, the right subtree of a node contains only nodes with keys strictly greater than the node's key, and both the left and right subtrees must also be binary search trees.

examples.explanation: The root node's value is 2, with left child 1 and right child 3, satisfying BST properties.
The root node's value is 5 but its right child's value is 4, which violates the BST rule.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 10^4].

title: Fraction to Recurring Decimal
description: Given two integers representing the numerator and denominator of a fraction, return the fraction in string format. If the fractional part is repeating, enclose the repeating part in parentheses. If multiple answers are possible, return any of them.

examples.explanation: 1 / 2 = 0.5 with no repeating part.
2 / 3 = 0.6666... where 6 repeats indefinitely.

title: Sequence Reconstruction
description: You are given an integer array nums of length n where nums is a permutation of the integers in the range [1, n]. You are also given a 2D integer array sequences where sequences[i] is a subsequence of nums. Check if nums is the shortest and the only sequence that can be uniquely reconstructed from the given sequences.

examples.explanation: There are two possible sequences that can be reconstructed: [1,2,3] and [1,3,2].
The only sequence that can be reconstructed is [1,2,3].

constraints: nums is a permutation of all the integers in the range [1, n].

title: The Latest Time to Catch a Bus
description: You are given a 0-indexed integer array buses of length n, where buses[i] represents the departure time of the ith bus. You are also given a 0-indexed integer array passengers of length m, where passengers[j] represents the arrival time of the jth passenger. All bus departure times and passenger arrival times are unique. You are given an integer capacity, which represents the maximum number of passengers that can get on each bus. Return the latest time you may arrive at the bus station to catch a bus without arriving at the same time as another passenger.

examples.explanation: Bus 1 takes passenger 2. Bus 2 takes passengers 17 and 18. Arriving at time 16 allows boarding before passenger 17.

constraints: All the values in buses and passengers are unique.

title: Divide Two Integers
description: Given two integers dividend and divisor, divide two integers without using multiplication, division, and mod operator. Return the quotient after dividing dividend by divisor. The integer division should truncate toward zero. If the quotient is strictly greater than 2^31 - 1, then return 2^31 - 1, and if it is strictly less than -2^31, then return -2^31.

examples.explanation: 10 / 3 = 3.33333... which is truncated to 3.
7 / -3 = -2.33333... which is truncated to -2.

title: Partition Array According to Given Pivot
description: You are given a 0-indexed integer array nums and an integer pivot. Rearrange nums such that: every element less than pivot appears before every element greater than pivot, every element equal to pivot appears between the elements less than and greater than pivot, and the relative order of the elements less than, equal to, and greater than pivot is maintained.

examples.explanation: Elements less than 10 are [9, 5, 3]. Elements equal to 10 are [10, 10]. Elements greater than 10 are [12, 14].

constraints: pivot equals to some element of nums.

title: Minimize Product Sum of Two Arrays
description: The product sum of two equal-length arrays A and B is equal to the sum of A[i] * B[i] for all 0 <= i < A.length. Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of length n, rearrange the elements of nums1 such that its product sum with nums2 is minimized. Return the minimum product sum.

examples.explanation: Rearrange nums1 to [5,4,3,2]. The product sum is 5*2 + 4*2 + 3*4 + 2*5 = 10 + 8 + 12 + 10 = 40.

title: Class Performance
description: Calculate the difference between the highest total score and the lowest total score among all students in a class. A student's total score is the sum of assignments, quizzes, and exams. Return the result table with the difference aliased as difference_in_score.

examples.explanation: Max total = 30 + 20 + 40 = 90. Min total = 10 + 10 + 20 = 40. Difference = 90 - 40 = 50.

constraints: student_id is the unique identifier for each student.

title: Find the Prefix Common Array of Two Arrays
description: You are given two 0-indexed integer permutations A and B of length n. A prefix common array of A and B is an array C such that C[i] is equal to the count of numbers that are present at or before the index i in both A and B. Return the prefix common array of A and B.

examples.explanation: At i = 0: no common elements. At i = 1: 1 and 3 are common (count 2). At i = 2: 1, 2, 3 are common (count 3). At i = 3: 1, 2, 3, 4 are common (count 4).

constraints: It is guaranteed that A and B are both permutations of n integers.

title: The k-th Lexicographical String of All Happy Strings of Length n
description: A happy string is a string that consists only of letters of the set ['a', 'b', 'c'] and does not have any two consecutive characters that are identical (s[i] != s[i + 1]). Given two integers n and k, consider a list of all happy strings of length n sorted in lexicographical order. Return the kth string of this list or return an empty string "" if there are less than k happy strings of length n.

examples.explanation: The happy strings of length 1 are ["a", "b", "c"]. The 3rd string is "c".
There are 12 happy strings of length 3. The 9th string is "cab".

title: Queries on Number of Points Inside a Circle
description: You are given an array points where points[i] = [x_i, y_i] is the coordinates of the ith point on a 2D plane. Multiple points can have the same coordinates. You are also given an array queries where queries[j] = [x_j, y_j, r_j] describes a circle centered at (x_j, y_j) with a radius of r_j. Return an array answer where answer[j] is the number of points that are inside the jth circle (including points on the border).

examples.explanation: The points inside the first circle are [1,3], [3,3], and [2,2].

title: Encode and Decode TinyURL
description: TinyURL is a URL shortening service. Design a system to encode a long URL to a tiny URL and decode a tiny URL to its original long URL. Implement the encode and decode methods without restrictions on formatting.

examples.explanation: Decoding the encoded string returns the original URL.

constraints: url is guaranteed to be a valid URL.

title: Deepest Leaves Sum
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the sum of values of its deepest leaves.

examples.explanation: The deepest leaves are nodes with values 7 and 8, and their sum is 15.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 10^4].

title: Spiral Matrix III
description: You start at the cell (rStart, cStart) of an rows x cols grid facing east. Walk in a clockwise spiral shape to visit every position in the grid. Return an array of coordinates representing the positions of the grid in the order they were visited.

examples.explanation: Spiral traversal inside a 1x4 matrix starting at (0,0).

title: Construct Binary Search Tree from Preorder Traversal
description: Given an array of integers preorder, which represents the preorder traversal of a binary search tree (BST), construct the tree and return its root.

examples.explanation: Constructed binary search tree matching the given preorder sequence.

constraints: All values of preorder are unique.

title: Find Elements in a Contaminated Binary Tree
description: Given a contaminated binary tree where all node values are -1, recover the tree such that the root value is 0, left child value is 2 * root.val + 1, and right child value is 2 * root.val + 2. Implement the FindElements class with a find(target) method that checks if target exists in the recovered tree.

examples.explanation: Root is 0, right child is 2. find(1) is false, find(2) is true.

constraints: The height of the binary tree is less than or equal to 20.
The total number of nodes is between [1, 10^4].
At most 10^4 calls will be made to find.

title: All People Report to the Given Manager
description: Write a solution to find employee_id of all employees that directly or indirectly report to the company head (employee_id = 1) with at most 3 levels of manager chain, excluding the head itself.

examples.explanation: All listed employees report to manager 1 in 3 or fewer jumps.

constraints: employee_id is the primary key for the Employees table.
Head of the company is the employee with employee_id = 1.

title: Create Binary Tree From Descriptions
description: You are given a 2D integer array descriptions where descriptions[i] = [parent_i, child_i, isLeft_i] indicates that parent_i is the parent of child_i in a binary tree of unique values, and isLeft_i == 1 indicates a left child. Construct the binary tree and return its root.

examples.explanation: Node 50 has no parent, so it is the root of the constructed binary tree.

constraints: The generated descriptions form a valid binary tree.

title: Arithmetic Subarrays
description: A sequence of numbers is called arithmetic if the difference between any two consecutive elements is the same. Given an array nums and two query arrays l and r of length m, return a boolean array of length m where answer[i] is true if the subarray nums[l[i]...r[i]] can be rearranged to form an arithmetic sequence.

examples.explanation: [4,6,5] can be rearranged to [4,5,6] (arithmetic). [4,6,5,9] cannot form an arithmetic progression. [5,9,3,7] can be rearranged to [3,5,7,9] (arithmetic).

title: Reveal Cards In Increasing Order
description: You are given an integer array deck. There is a deck where every card has a unique integer. Reorder the deck such that when revealing cards repeatedly by taking the top card and moving the next card to the bottom, the cards are revealed in increasing order.

examples.explanation: Revealing the cards one by one produces sequence [2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17].

constraints: All the values of deck are unique.

title: Letter Tile Possibilities
description: You have n tiles, where each tile has one letter tiles[i] printed on it. Return the number of possible non-empty sequences of letters you can make using the letters printed on those tiles.

examples.explanation: The possible sequences are "A", "B", "AA", "AB", "BA", "AAB", "ABA", "BAA".
Total number of non-empty distinct arrangements.

constraints: tiles consists of uppercase English letters.

title: All Possible Full Binary Trees
description: Given an integer n, return a list of all possible full binary trees with n nodes. Each node of each tree in the answer must have Node.val == 0. A full binary tree is a binary tree where each node has exactly 0 or 2 children.

examples.explanation: There are 5 possible full binary trees with 7 nodes.

title: Find Valid Matrix Given Row and Column Sums
description: You are given two arrays rowSum and colSum of non-negative integers where rowSum[i] is the sum of the elements in the ith row and colSum[j] is the sum of the elements in the jth column. Find any 2D non-negative matrix of size rowSum.length x colSum.length that satisfies the row and column sums.

examples.explanation: Row sums are [3, 8] and column sums are [4, 7].

title: Minimum Number of Vertices to Reach All Nodes
description: Given a directed acyclic graph, with n vertices numbered from 0 to n-1, and an array edges where edges[i] = [from_i, to_i] represents a directed edge from from_i to to_i. Find the smallest set of vertices from which all nodes in the graph are reachable.

examples.explanation: Nodes 0 and 3 have in-degree 0 and can reach every other node in the graph.

title: Find the Punishment Number of an Integer
description: Given a positive integer n, return the punishment number of n. The punishment number of n is defined as the sum of the squares of all integers i such that 1 <= i <= n and the decimal representation of i * i can be partitioned into contiguous substrings whose integer values add up to i.

title: Count Number of Distinct Integers After Reverse Operations
description: You are given an array nums consisting of positive integers. Take each integer in the array, reverse its digits, and append the reversed integer to the end of the array. Return the number of distinct integers in the final array.

examples.explanation: After reversing and appending, array is [1, 13, 10, 12, 31, 1, 31, 1, 21, 13]. Distinct values are [1, 10, 12, 13, 21, 31].

title: Find Leaves of Binary Tree
description: Given the root of a binary tree, collect a tree's nodes as if you were doing this: collect all the leaf nodes, remove all leaves, repeat until the tree is empty.

examples.explanation: First round leaves are [4,5,3], second round leave is [2], last remaining root is [1].

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 100].

title: Longest Common Subsequence Between Sorted Arrays
description: Given an array of integer arrays arrays where each arrays[i] is sorted in strictly increasing order, return an integer array representing the longest common subsequence present in all arrays.

examples.explanation: The elements 1 and 4 appear in all given arrays.

constraints: arrays[i] is sorted in strictly increasing order.

title: Build an Array With Stack Operations
description: You are given an integer array target and an integer n. You have an empty stack and an input stream of integers from 1 to n. Read numbers sequentially: apply "Push" to push to the stack, or "Pop" to discard the top element. Return the stack operations needed to build target.

examples.explanation: Read 1: Push -> Stack [1]. Read 2: Push, Pop -> Stack [1]. Read 3: Push -> Stack [1,3].

title: Largest Submatrix With Rearrangements
description: You are given a binary matrix matrix of size m x n, and you are allowed to rearrange the columns of the matrix in any order. Return the area of the largest submatrix within matrix where every element of the submatrix is 1 after reordering the columns optimally.

examples.explanation: Rearrange columns 1 and 2 to form a 2x2 square submatrix of all 1s.

title: Watering Plants
description: You want to water n plants in your garden with a watering can of capacity capacity. Plants are placed along a line at indices 0 to n-1. The river is located at index -1. If you cannot completely water the next plant, you must return to the river to refill. Return the total number of steps to water all plants.

examples.explanation: Steps taken to water plants and refill at river when capacity is exhausted.

title: Check if Number is a Sum of Powers of Three
description: Given an integer n, return true if it is possible to represent n as the sum of distinct powers of three. Otherwise, return false.

examples.explanation: 21 cannot be represented as a sum of distinct powers of 3.

title: Divide Array Into Arrays With Max Difference
description: You are given an integer array nums of size n and a positive integer k. Divide the array into n / 3 arrays of size 3 such that the difference between any two elements in one array is less than or equal to k. Return a 2D array containing all the arrays, or an empty array if impossible.

examples.explanation: The difference between any two elements in each array is <= 2.

title: Remove Sub-Folders from the Filesystem
description: Given a list of folders folder, return the folders after removing all sub-folders in those folders. A sub-folder of folder[i] is located within folder[i] and has its path starting with folder[i] followed by "/".

examples.explanation: "/a/b" is a sub-folder of "/a" and "/c/d/e" is a sub-folder of "/c/d".

constraints: folder[i] contains only lowercase letters and '/'.
folder[i] always starts with the character '/'.

title: Find Root of N-Ary Tree
description: You are given all the nodes of an N-ary tree as an array of Node objects, where each node has a unique value. The tree is not given starting from the root. Find and return the root of the N-ary tree using O(1) additional space.

examples.explanation: Node with value 1 has in-degree 0 and is the root.

constraints: The total number of nodes is between [1, 5 * 10^4].
Each node has a unique value.

title: Remove All Occurrences of a Substring
description: Given two strings s and part, perform the following operation on s until all occurrences of the substring part are removed: Find the leftmost occurrence of the substring part and remove it from s. Return s after all occurrences of part have been removed.

examples.explanation: Remove "abc" from index 2 -> "dabaabcbc", remove "abc" from index 4 -> "dababc", remove "abc" from index 3 -> "dab".

constraints: s and part consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Design Most Recently Used Queue
description: Design a queue-like data structure that moves the most recently used elements to the end of the queue. Implement the MRUQueue class with fetch(k) which moves the kth element (1-indexed) to the end of the queue and returns it.

examples.explanation: Starting queue [1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8]. fetch(3) returns 3, queue becomes [1,2,4,5,6,7,8,3].

constraints: At most 2000 calls will be made to fetch.

title: Binary Tree Nodes
description: You are given a table Tree with columns N (node value) and P (parent value). Write a query to find the node type of Binary Tree ordered by the value of the node: 'Root' if the node is root, 'Leaf' if the node is a leaf, and 'Inner' if the node is neither root nor leaf.

examples.explanation: Node 5 has no parent (Root), nodes 2 and 8 have children and a parent (Inner), others are Leaves.

constraints: N is the primary key for the table.
Each row in Tree indicates node N and its parent node P.

title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Postorder Traversal
description: Given two integer arrays, preorder and postorder where preorder is the preorder traversal of a binary tree of distinct values and postorder is the postorder traversal of the same tree, reconstruct and return the binary tree.

examples.explanation: Constructed binary tree matches both preorder and postorder sequences.

constraints: All the values of preorder are unique.
All the values of postorder are unique.

title: Convert Object to JSON String
description: Given an object, return a valid JSON string of that object. You should implement the function without using the built-in JSON.stringify method.

examples.explanation: Object converted into a serialized JSON string.
Array serialized into JSON array format.

constraints: object is a valid JSON value (null, boolean, number, string, array, or object)

title: Output Contest Matches
description: During the NBA playoffs, we always arrange the rather strong team to play with the rather weak team, like make the rank 1 team play with the rank nth team. Given n teams, return their contest matches in string format representing pairings by parentheses.

examples.explanation: Round 1 pairs: (1,4), (2,3). Round 2 combines them to ((1,4),(2,3)).
Successive tournament match combinations.

constraints: n == 2^k where k is in the range [1, 12].

title: Regions Cut By Slashes
description: An n x n grid is composed of 1 x 1 squares where each 1 x 1 square consists of a '/', '\', or blank space ' '. These characters divide the square into contiguous regions. Given the grid represented as a string array, return the number of regions.

examples.explanation: The 2x2 grid is divided into 2 distinct contiguous regions.
Slanted lines split the grid into 5 regions.

title: Partition Array for Maximum Sum
description: Given an integer array arr, partition the array into (contiguous) subarrays of length at most k. After partitioning, each subarray has their values changed to become the maximum value of that subarray. Return the largest sum of the given array after partitioning.

title: Distribute Coins in Binary Tree
description: You are given the root of a binary tree with n nodes where each node in the tree has node.val coins. There are n coins in whole tree in total. In one move, we may choose two adjacent nodes and move one coin from one node to another. Return the minimum number of moves required to make every node have exactly one coin.

examples.explanation: From the root, move one coin to its left child, and one coin to its right child.
From the left child, move two coins to root, then move one coin to right child.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is n.
The sum of all Node.val is n.

title: Subdomain Visit Count
description: A website domain like "discuss.leetcode.com" consists of various subdomains. Given an array of count-paired domains cpdomains, return the visit counts of each subdomain in the input. You may return the answer in any order.

examples.explanation: "discuss.leetcode.com" visits: "discuss.leetcode.com" (9001), "leetcode.com" (9001), and "com" (9001).

constraints: cpdomains[i] follows either the "rep d1.d2.d3" or "rep d1.d2" format.
rep is an integer in the range [1, 10^4].

title: Binary Search Tree Iterator
description: Implement the BSTIterator class that represents an iterator over the in-order traversal of a binary search tree (BST). next() returns the next smallest number and hasNext() returns whether we have a next number in O(1) average time and O(h) memory.

examples.explanation: Traverses binary search tree nodes in sorted order.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 10^5].
At most 10^5 calls will be made to hasNext, and next.

title: Matrix Block Sum
description: Given a m x n matrix mat and an integer k, return a matrix answer where each answer[i][j] is the sum of all elements mat[r][c] for: i - k <= r <= i + k, j - k <= c <= j + k, and (r, c) is a valid position in the matrix.

examples.explanation: Calculates local neighborhood sum for each block within radius k.

title: Lexicographical Numbers
description: Given an integer n, return all the numbers in the range [1, n] sorted in lexicographical order. You must write an algorithm that runs in O(n) time and uses O(1) extra space.

examples.explanation: Numbers 1 through 13 ordered alphabetically like strings.
Alphabetical order of 1 to 2.

title: Remove All Ones With Row and Column Flips
description: You are given an m x n binary matrix grid. In one operation, you can choose any row or column and flip each of its values (0 to 1, or 1 to 0). Return true if it is possible to remove all 1's from grid using any number of operations, or false otherwise.

examples.explanation: Flip row 1, then flip column 1. The matrix becomes all 0s.
It is impossible to make all values equal to 0.

title: Map of Highest Peak
description: You are given an m x n integer matrix isWater where isWater[i][j] == 1 if cell is water and 0 if land. Assign each cell a height such that water cells have height 0 and the absolute difference in height between two adjacent cells is at most 1. Return an matrix height containing the assigned heights maximizing the peak.

examples.explanation: Water cell at (0,1) gets 0. Land cells get valid maximum incremental heights.

constraints: There is at least one water cell.

title: Spiral Matrix II
description: Given a positive integer n, generate an n x n matrix filled with elements from 1 to n^2 in spiral order.

examples.explanation: Values 1 to 9 populated clockwise in spiral form.
A 1x1 matrix with single element 1.

title: Count Number of Nice Subarrays
description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer k. A continuous subarray is called nice if there are k odd numbers on it. Return the number of nice sub-arrays.

examples.explanation: The only sub-arrays with 3 odd numbers are [1,1,2,1] and [1,2,1,1].
There are no odd numbers in the array, so no nice subarray exists.

title: Find Nearest Right Node in Binary Tree
description: Given the root of a binary tree and a node u in the tree, return the nearest node on the same level that is to the right of u, or return null if u is the rightmost node in its level.

examples.explanation: The nearest node to the right of node 4 on the same depth is node 5.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 10^5].
All values in the tree are distinct.
u is a node in the given binary tree.

title: Change the Root of a Binary Tree
description: Given the root of a binary tree and a leaf node, reroot the tree so that leaf becomes the new root. You can flip the direction of edge from parent to child to achieve this. Return the new root of the tree.

examples.explanation: Leaf 7 becomes root, parent pointers are reversed accordingly.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [2, 100].
leaf is a leaf in the tree.

title: Queue Reconstruction by Height
description: You are given an array of people, people, where people[i] = [h_i, k_i] represents the ith person of height h_i with exactly k_i other people in front who have a height greater than or equal to h_i. Reconstruct and return the queue that satisfies everyone's attributes.

examples.explanation: Person [5,0] has 0 taller/equal ahead. Person [7,0] has 0 taller/equal ahead. Person [5,2] has [5,0] and [7,0] ahead.

constraints: It is guaranteed that the queue can be reconstructed.

title: Exchange Seats
description: Write a solution to swap the seat id of every two consecutive students from the Seat table. If the number of students is odd, the id of the last student is not swapped. Return the result table ordered by id in ascending order.

examples.explanation: Seats 1 and 2 swap, seats 3 and 4 swap, and seat 5 stays the same.

constraints: id is the primary key for Seat table.
id is a continuous incrementing sequence.

title: Number of Substrings Containing All Three Characters
description: Given a string s consisting only of characters a, b and c, return the number of substrings containing at least one occurrence of all these characters a, b and c.

examples.explanation: Substrings containing 'a', 'b' and 'c' at least once are "abc", "abca", "abcab", "abcabc", "bca", "bcab", "bcabc", "cab", "cabc", and "abc".

constraints: s only consists of a, b or c characters.

title: Sum of Beauty of All Substrings
description: The beauty of a string is the difference in frequencies between the most frequent and least frequent characters. Given a string s, return the sum of beauty of all of its substrings.

examples.explanation: The substrings with non-zero beauty are ["aab","aabc","aabcb","abcb","bcb"], each with beauty 1.

constraints: s consists of only lowercase English letters.

title: Minimum Add to Make Parentheses Valid
description: A parentheses string is valid if and only if: it is the empty string, it can be written as AB, or it can be written as (A). Given a parentheses string s, return the minimum number of moves required to make s valid (inserting '(' or ')' anywhere).

examples.explanation: One additional '(' is needed at the front.
Three additional ')' are needed at the end.

title: Correct a Binary Tree
description: You have a binary tree with a node whose right pointer erroneously points to another node on the same depth to its right. Given the root of this defective tree, return the root of the tree after removing the node with the invalid right pointer and its entire subtree.

examples.explanation: Node 5 has invalid right child pointer to node 6 on the same level. Node 5 and its descendants are removed.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [2, 10^4].
The defective node and erroneous connection are guaranteed to exist.

title: Unique Length-3 Palindromic Subsequences
description: Given a string s, return the number of unique palindromes of length three that are a subsequence of s. Note that even if there are multiple ways to obtain the same subsequence, it is still only counted once.

examples.explanation: The 3 palindromic subsequences of length 3 are: "aba", "aaa", and "aca".
The 4 palindromic subsequences of length 3 are: "bbb", "bcb", "bab", and "aba".

constraints: s consists of only lowercase English letters.

title: Increment Submatrices by One
description: You are given a positive integer n, indicating that we initially have an n x n 0-indexed integer matrix mat filled with zeroes. You are also given a 2D integer array queries where queries[i] = [row1_i, col1_i, row2_i, col2_i]. For each query, you should add 1 to every element in the submatrix with top-left corner (row1_i, col1_i) and bottom-right corner (row2_i, col2_i). Return the matrix mat after performing every query.

examples.explanation: Matrix after applying both 2D range increment queries.
Every element in the 2x2 matrix is incremented by 1.

title: Insert into a Binary Search Tree
description: You are given the root node of a binary search tree (BST) and a value to insert into the tree. Return the root node of the BST after the insertion. It is guaranteed that the new value does not exist in the original BST. Notice that there may exist multiple valid ways for the insertion, as long as the tree remains a BST after insertion.

examples.explanation: 5 is inserted as the left child of node 7.
25 is inserted as the left child of node 30.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree will be in the range [0, 10^4].
All the values Node.val are unique.
It's guaranteed that val does not exist in the original BST.

title: Stone Game
description: Alice and Bob play a game with piles of stones. There are an even number of piles arranged in a row, and each pile has a positive integer number of stones piles[i]. The total number of stones across all the piles is odd, so there are no ties. Players take turns taking either the first or the last pile from the row. Assuming Alice and Bob play optimally, return true if Alice wins the game, or false if Bob wins.

examples.explanation: Alice can always choose piles to ensure obtaining strictly more stones than Bob.
Alice starts first and wins with optimal strategy.

title: Count Servers that Communicate
description: You are given a map of a server center, represented as a m * n integer matrix grid, where 1 means that on that cell there is a server and 0 means that it is empty. Two servers are said to communicate if they are on the same row or on the same column. Return the number of servers that communicate with at least one other server.

examples.explanation: No servers can communicate with each other because no two servers share the same row or column.
All three servers can communicate with at least one other server.

title: Different Ways to Add Parentheses
description: Given a string expression of numbers and operators, return all possible results from computing all the different possible ways to group numbers and operators. You may return the answer in any order. The valid operators are '+', '-', and '*'.

examples.explanation: All distinct parenthesis groupings yield these arithmetic results.

constraints: expression consists of digits and the operator '+', '-', and '*'.
All integer values in the input expression are in the range [0, 99].

title: Words Within Two Edits of Dictionary
description: You are given two string arrays, queries and dictionary, where all strings are of the same length. In one edit you can change a character of a word to any other character. Return all words in queries that match some word in dictionary with at most two edits. Return the words in the same order they appear in queries.

examples.explanation: "word" can be edited to "wood" in 1 edit. "note" can be edited to "joke" in 2 edits. "wood" matches exactly in 0 edits.

constraints: All queries[i] and dictionary[j] consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Find the City With the Smallest Number of Neighbors at a Threshold Distance
description: There are n cities numbered from 0 to n-1. Given the array edges where edges[i] = [from_i, to_i, weight_i] and an integer distanceThreshold. Return the city with the smallest number of cities that are reachable through some path and whose distance is at most distanceThreshold. If there are multiple such cities, return the city with the greatest number.

examples.explanation: City 0 has 2 neighbors, city 1 has 3 neighbors, city 2 has 3 neighbors, city 3 has 2 neighbors within distance <= 4. City 3 is chosen as the tie-breaker.

title: Range Addition
description: You are given an integer length and an array updates where updates[i] = [startIdx_i, endIdx_i, inc_i]. You have an array arr of length length with all zeros. Apply all updates by incrementing arr[startIdx_i...endIdx_i] by inc_i and return the modified array.

examples.explanation: Initial: [0,0,0,0,0] -> after update 1: [0,2,2,2,0] -> after update 2: [0,2,5,5,3] -> after update 3: [-2,0,3,5,3].

title: Search in a Sorted Array of Unknown Size
description: This is an interactive problem. You have a sorted array of unique elements and an unknown size. You can only access the array using an ArrayReader interface: reader.get(k) returns the value at index k (0-indexed) or 2^31 - 1 if k is out of bounds. Given target, return its index or -1 if target is not in the array in O(log n) time.

examples.explanation: 9 exists in secret and its index is 4.
2 does not exist in secret so return -1.

constraints: secret is sorted in a strictly increasing order.

title: Interval List Intersections
description: You are given two lists of closed intervals, firstList and secondList, where firstList[i] = [start_i, end_i] and secondList[j] = [start_j, end_j]. Each list of intervals is pairwise disjoint and in sorted order. Return the intersection of these two interval lists.

examples.explanation: The closed intervals where both lists overlap.

title: Game of Life
description: According to Conway's Game of Life, given a board of m x n cells (each 0 or 1), calculate the next state of the board simultaneously based on standard neighbor rules (under-population, survival, over-population, reproduction). You must solve it in-place.

examples.explanation: All cells are evaluated simultaneously based on their 8 neighbors.

title: Iterator for Combination
description: Design the CombinationIterator class that supports next() returning the next combination of length combinationLength in lexicographical order, and hasNext() returning true if and only if there exists a next combination.

examples.explanation: Generates all combinations of length 2 from "abc" in sorted order.

constraints: All characters in characters are unique and lowercase English letters.
At most 10^4 calls will be made to next and hasNext.

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Reinitialize a Permutation
description: You are given an even integer n. You have an initial permutation perm where perm[i] == i. In each operation, a new array arr is created where arr[i] = perm[i / 2] if i % 2 == 0, or arr[i] = perm[n / 2 + (i - 1) / 2] if i % 2 == 1. Return the minimum non-zero number of operations to return perm to its initial state.

examples.explanation: Initial: [0,1]. After 1 operation: arr[0]=perm[0]=0, arr[1]=perm[1]=1. Total 1 step.

title: Where Will the Ball Fall
description: You have a 2D grid of size m x n representing a box. Each cell contains a diagonal board: 1 spans top-left to bottom-right, and -1 spans top-right to bottom-left. Drop n balls at the top of each column. Return an array answer where answer[i] is the column where the ith ball falls out at the bottom, or -1 if the ball gets stuck.

examples.explanation: Ball 0 exits at column 1. All other balls get stuck in V-shaped traps.

title: Longest Word With All Prefixes
description: Given an array of strings words, find the longest string in words such that every prefix of it is also in words. If there is more than one string with the same maximum length, return the lexicographically smallest one. If no such string exists, return "".

examples.explanation: "kiran" has prefixes "k", "ki", "kir", "kira", all present in words.
Both "apple" and "apply" have all prefixes present. "apple" is lexicographically smaller.

constraints: words[i] consists only of lowercase English letters.

title: Number of Enclaves
description: You are given an m x n binary matrix grid, where 0 represents water and 1 represents land. A move consists of walking from one land cell to an adjacent 4-directionally land cell or walking off the boundary of the grid. Return the number of land cells in grid for which we cannot walk off the boundary of the grid in any number of moves.

examples.explanation: Three 1s in the center are surrounded by 0s and cannot walk off the boundary.

title: Minimum Cost to Connect Sticks
description: You have some number of sticks with positive integer lengths. You can connect any two sticks of lengths x and y into one stick by paying a cost of x + y. You perform this until there is only one stick remaining. Return the minimum cost to connect all the given sticks into one stick in this way.

examples.explanation: Connect 2 and 3 (cost 5) -> [4, 5]. Connect 4 and 5 (cost 9) -> [9]. Total cost = 5 + 9 = 14.
Connect 1 and 3 (cost 4) -> [4,5,8]. Connect 4 and 5 (cost 9) -> [9,8]. Connect 8 and 9 (cost 17) -> [17]. Total cost = 30.

title: Minimum Adjacent Swaps to Reach the Kth Smallest Number
description: You are given a string num, representing a large integer, and an integer k. We call a string wonderful if it is a permutation of the digits in num and is greater than num. Return the minimum number of adjacent digit swaps to reach the kth smallest wonderful integer from num.

examples.explanation: The 4th smallest wonderful integer is "5489355421". It requires 2 adjacent swaps to reach it from num.

title: Sort Integers by The Power Value
description: The power of an integer x is the number of steps to transform x into 1 using Collatz operations (if even x = x / 2; if odd x = 3 * x + 1). Given lo, hi and k, sort all integers in the range [lo, hi] by their power value in ascending order (break ties by integer value). Return the kth integer in this sorted list.

examples.explanation: Power values: 12->9, 13->9, 14->17, 15->17. Sorted list: [12, 13, 14, 15]. The 2nd element is 13.

title: Number of Good Leaf Nodes Pairs
description: You are given the root of a binary tree and an integer distance. A pair of two different leaf nodes of a binary tree is said to be good if the length of the shortest path between them is less than or equal to distance. Return the number of good leaf node pairs in the tree.

examples.explanation: The leaf nodes are 4 and 3, and the shortest path between them is 3, which is <= distance.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 2^10].

title: Check If Two Expression Trees are Equivalent
description: A binary expression tree is a tree whose leaves are lowercase letters representing variables and internal nodes are '+' operations. Given roots root1 and root2 of two binary expression trees, return true if the two expression trees evaluate to the same algebraic expression.

examples.explanation: Both trees represent the commutative expression a + b + c.

constraints: The number of nodes in both trees is in the range [1, 4999].
Node.val is either '+' or a lowercase English letter.
Every internal node has exactly two children.

title: Minimum Remove to Make Valid Parentheses
description: Given a string s of '(' , ')' and lowercase English characters. Remove the minimum number of parentheses ('(' or ')', in any positions) so that the resulting parentheses string is valid and return any valid string.

examples.explanation: "lee(t(c)ode)" or "lee(t(co)de)" would also be accepted.
Remove the invalid leading ')'.

constraints: s[i] is either '(' , ')', or a lowercase English letter.

title: Longest Subarray of 1's After Deleting One Element
description: Given a binary array nums, you should delete one element from it. Return the size of the longest non-empty subarray containing only 1's in the resulting array. Return 0 if there is no such subarray.

examples.explanation: After deleting the number at index 2, [1,1,1] contains 3 numbers with value 1's.
After deleting the number at index 4, [1,1,1,1,1] results in length 5.

title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
description: You are given an array points representing integer coordinates of some points on a 2D-plane, where points[i] = [x_i, y_i]. The cost of connecting two points [x_i, y_i] and [x_j, y_j] is the Manhattan distance between them: |x_i - x_j| + |y_i - y_j|. Return the minimum cost to make all points connected such that there is exactly one simple path between any two points.

examples.explanation: Connect points to form a minimum spanning tree with total Manhattan edge cost 20.

title: Count Submatrices With All Ones
description: Given an m x n binary matrix mat, return the number of submatrices that have all ones.

examples.explanation: There are 6 rectangles of size 1x1, 2 of size 1x2, 3 of size 2x1, 1 of size 2x2, and 1 of size 3x1. Total = 13.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
description: Given a binary search tree (BST), find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) node of two given nodes in the BST. According to the definition of LCA on Wikipedia: The lowest common ancestor is defined between two nodes p and q as the lowest node in T that has both p and q as descendants (where we allow a node to be a descendant of itself).

examples.explanation: The LCA of nodes 2 and 8 is 6.
The LCA of nodes 2 and 4 is 2, since a node can be a descendant of itself according to the LCA definition.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [2, 10^5].
p and q will exist in the BST.

title: Maximum Absolute Sum of Any Subarray
description: You are given an integer array nums. The absolute sum of a subarray [nums[l], nums[l+1], ..., nums[r-1], nums[r]] is abs(nums[l] + nums[l+1] + ... + nums[r-1] + nums[r]). Return the maximum absolute sum of any (possibly empty) subarray of nums.

examples.explanation: The subarray [2,3] has the maximum absolute sum abs(2+3) = abs(5) = 5.
The subarray [-5,1,-4] has the maximum absolute sum abs(-5+1-4) = abs(-8) = 8.

title: Fill a Special Grid
description: You are given an integer n. You need to construct an n x n grid filled with numbers according to specific placement and symmetry constraints such that each row and column fulfills balance conditions. Return any valid grid satisfying the constraints.

examples.explanation: The grid satisfies all symmetry and placement conditions.

title: The kth Factor of n
description: You are given two positive integers n and k. A factor of an integer n is defined as an integer i where n % i == 0. Consider a list of all factors of n sorted in ascending order, return the kth factor in this list or return -1 if n has less than k factors.

examples.explanation: Factors list is [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12], the 3rd factor is 3.
Factors list is [1, 7], the 2nd factor is 7.
Factors list is [1, 2, 4], there is no 4th factor so return -1.

title: Find Champion II
description: There are n teams numbered from 0 to n - 1 in a tournament. You are given a 2D integer array edges of length m representing DAG directed edges, where edges[i] = [u_i, v_i] indicates that team u_i is stronger than team v_i. Return the team that will be the champion of the tournament if there is a unique champion, otherwise, return -1.

examples.explanation: Team 0 defeats team 1, and team 1 defeats team 2. Team 0 is the unique champion.
Both team 0 and team 1 have no incoming edges, so a unique champion cannot be determined.

constraints: All edges are distinct and the input is a valid DAG.

title: Sum Root to Leaf Numbers
description: You are given the root of a binary tree containing digits from 0 to 9 only. Each root-to-leaf path in the tree represents a number. For example, the root-to-leaf path 1 -> 2 -> 3 represents the number 123. Return the total sum of all root-to-leaf numbers. Test cases are generated so that the answer will fit in a 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: The root-to-leaf path 1->2 represents 12. The root-to-leaf path 1->3 represents 13. Total sum = 12 + 13 = 25.
The root-to-leaf path 4->9->5 represents 495. The root-to-leaf path 4->9->1 represents 491. The root-to-leaf path 4->0 represents 40. Total sum = 495 + 491 + 40 = 1026.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 1000].
The depth of the tree will not exceed 10.

title: Find Positive Integer Solution for a Given Equation
description: Given a callable function f(x, y) with a hidden formula and a value z, reverse engineer the formula and return all positive integer pairs (x, y) where f(x, y) == z. The function is strictly increasing with respect to both x and y (i.e., f(x+1, y) > f(x, y) and f(x, y+1) > f(x, y)). Return the list of pairs sorted in ascending order by x.

examples.explanation: The hidden formula is f(x, y) = x + y. Solutions for x + y = 5 are (1,4), (2,3), (3,2), (4,1).
The hidden formula is f(x, y) = x * y. Solutions for x * y = 5 are (1,5), (5,1).

constraints: The output pairs are valid positive integers within range.

title: Simplified Fractions
description: Given an integer n, return a list of all simplified fractions between 0 and 1 (exclusive) such that the denominator is less than or equal to n. You can return the answer in any order.

examples.explanation: Only "1/2" has denominator <= 2 and is irreducible.
"2/4" is not simplified, it can be simplified to "1/2".

title: Tuple with Same Product
description: Given an array nums of distinct positive integers, return the number of tuples (a, b, c, d) such that a * b = c * d where a, b, c, and d are elements of nums, and a != b != c != d.

examples.explanation: There are 16 valid tuples satisfying the condition.

constraints: All elements in nums are distinct.

title: Number of Zero-Filled Subarrays
description: Given an integer array nums, return the number of subarrays filled with 0. A zero-filled subarray is a contiguous sequence of elements consisting only of the number 0.

examples.explanation: Subarrays of 0s: four of length 1 and two of length 2. Total = 6.
Subarrays of length 1: 5, length 2: 3, length 3: 1. Total = 9.

title: Maximum Level Sum of a Binary Tree
description: Given the root of a binary tree, the level of its root is 1, the level of its children is 2, and so on. Return the smallest level x such that the sum of all the values of nodes at level x is maximal.

examples.explanation: Level 1 sum = 1. Level 2 sum = 7 + 0 = 7. Level 3 sum = 7 + (-8) = -1. Level 2 produces maximum sum.
Level 2 yields the maximum level sum.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 10^4].

title: Maximum Length of Semi-Decreasing Subarrays
description: You are given an integer array nums. Return the length of the longest semi-decreasing subarray of nums. A subarray nums[i...j] is semi-decreasing if i < j and nums[i] > nums[j]. If no such subarray exists, return 0.

examples.explanation: The entire array nums[0...6] is semi-decreasing because nums[0] = 7 > nums[6] = 1.
No pair satisfies i < j and nums[i] > nums[j].

title: Beautiful Array
description: An array nums of length n is beautiful if: nums is a permutation of integers from 1 to n, and for every 0 <= i < j < n, there is no index k with i < k < j such that 2 * nums[k] == nums[i] + nums[j]. Given integer n, return any beautiful array nums of length n.

examples.explanation: [1,3,2,4] is also a valid beautiful array.
All valid pairings avoid arithmetic midpoint violations.

title: Evaluate the Bracket Pairs of a String
description: You are given a string s that contains some bracket pairs, with each key enclosed in parentheses '(key)', and a 2D string array knowledge where knowledge[i] = [key_i, value_i]. Replace each bracket pair with its matching value from knowledge. If the key is not in knowledge, replace the bracket pair with '?'. Return the resulting string.

examples.explanation: The key "name" has value "bob", and key "age" has value "two".
"name" is not present in knowledge, so it is replaced with "?".

constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters and brackets '(' and ')'.
Every open bracket '(' in s will have a matching close bracket ')'.

title: Swapping Nodes in a Linked List
description: You are given the head of a linked list, and an integer k. Return the head of the linked list after swapping the values of the kth node from the beginning and the kth node from the end (the list is 1-indexed).

examples.explanation: Swap the 2nd node from beginning (value 2) and 2nd node from end (value 4).
The 5th node from beginning and end are swapped.

constraints: The number of nodes in the list is n.

title: Minimize Hamming Distance After Swap Operations
description: You are given two integer arrays, source and target, both of length n. You are also given a 2D integer array allowedSwaps where each allowedSwaps[i] = [a_i, b_i] allows swapping the elements at indices a_i and b_i any number of times. Return the minimum Hamming distance between source and target after applying any sequence of swaps.

examples.explanation: Swap indices 0 and 1 -> [2,1,3,4]. The Hamming distance with target is 1 (due to mismatch at index 3: 4 vs 5).
No swaps are allowed, 2 mismatches exist.

title: Flip Equivalent Binary Trees
description: For a binary tree T, we can define a flip operation as follows: choose any node, and swap the left and right child subtrees. A binary tree X is flip equivalent to a binary tree Y if and only if we can make X equal to Y after some number of flip operations. Given the roots of two binary trees root1 and root2, return true if the two trees are flip equivalent, or false otherwise.

examples.explanation: We flipped at nodes with values 1, 3, and 5.
Two empty trees are flip equivalent.

constraints: The number of nodes in each tree is in the range [0, 100].
Each tree will have unique node values in the range [0, 99].

title: K Closest Points to Origin
description: Given an array of points where points[i] = [x_i, y_i] represents a point on the X-Y plane and an integer k, return the k closest points to the origin (0, 0). The distance between two points on the X-Y plane is the Euclidean distance (i.e., sqrt((x1 - x2)^2 + (y1 - y2)^2)). You may return the answer in any order.

examples.explanation: Distance of (1, 3) is sqrt(10). Distance of (-2, 2) is sqrt(8). Since sqrt(8) < sqrt(10), [-2, 2] is closer.
The 2 points closest to the origin are [3,3] and [-2,4].

title: Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet
description: A triplet is an array of three integers. You are given a 2D integer array triplets, where triplets[i] = [a_i, b_i, c_i] describes the ith triplet. You are also given an integer array target = [x, y, z]. To update an existing triplet, you can choose two indices i and j and update triplets[j] to become [max(a_i, a_j), max(b_i, b_j), max(c_i, c_j)]. Return true if it is possible to obtain target as an element of triplets, or false otherwise.

examples.explanation: Merge triplets[0] and triplets[2] -> [max(2,1), max(5,7), max(3,5)] = [2,7,5].
It is impossible to obtain [3,2,5] because every choice exceeds target values.

title: Construct Binary Tree from Inorder and Postorder Traversal
description: Given two integer arrays inorder and postorder where inorder is the inorder traversal of a binary tree and postorder is the postorder traversal of the same tree, construct and return the binary tree.

examples.explanation: The reconstructed binary tree root is 3, left child 9, right subtree contains 20 with children 15 and 7.
Single node binary tree.

constraints: inorder and postorder consist of unique values.
Each value of postorder also appears in inorder.

title: Guess the Majority in a Hidden Array
description: This is an interactive problem. An array reader provides an API query(a, b, c, d) that returns 4 if all elements are equal, 2 if three are equal, and 0 if two are equal. Given the length of the array n, find the index of any element with the majority count in the hidden array, or -1 if no majority element exists.

examples.explanation: 1 is the majority element (appears 5 times). Index 5 has value 1.

constraints: At most 2 * n calls will be made to query.

title: Split a String Into the Max Number of Unique Substrings
description: Given a string s, return the maximum number of unique substrings that the given string can be split into. You can split string s into any list of non-empty substrings, where the concatenation of the substrings forms the original string, and all split substrings must be mutually distinct.

examples.explanation: One valid split is ["a", "b", "ab", "c", "cc"] which gives 5 unique substrings.
One valid split is ["a", "ba"].

constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters.

title: Maximum Score From Removing Stones
description: You are playing a solitaire game with three piles of stones of sizes a, b, and c respectively. Each turn you choose two non-empty piles, remove 1 stone from each, and add 1 point to your score. The game stops when there are fewer than two non-empty piles. Given three integers a, b, and c, return the maximum score you can get.

examples.explanation: The optimal sequence of takes yields a score of 6.
Max points obtainable from the three piles is 7.

title: Filling Bookcase Shelves
description: You are given an array books where books[i] = [thickness_i, height_i] and an integer shelfWidth. We want to place these books in order onto bookcase shelves of fixed width shelfWidth. The height of each shelf is the maximum height of the books placed on it. Return the minimum possible total height of the bookshelf after placing all books.

title: Wiggle Sort
description: Given an integer array nums, reorder it in-place such that nums[0] <= nums[1] >= nums[2] <= nums[3]... You may assume the array always has a valid answer.

examples.explanation: [1,6,2,5,3,4] is also a valid wiggle sorted array.
The reordering satisfies the alternating inequality condition.

title: Path with Maximum Gold
description: In a gold mine grid of size m x n, each cell in this mine has an integer representing the amount of gold in that cell, 0 if it is empty. Return the maximum amount of gold you can collect under the conditions: every time you are located in a cell you will collect all the gold in that cell, from your position you can walk one step to the left, right, up, or down, you cannot visit the same cell more than once, never visit a cell with 0 gold, and you can start and stop collecting gold from any position in the grid that has some gold.

examples.explanation: Path to get the maximum gold, 9 -> 8 -> 7.

constraints: There are at most 25 cells containing gold.

title: Number of Good Ways to Split a String
description: You are given a string s. A split is called good if you can split s into two non-empty strings s_left and s_right such that their concatenation is equal to s and the number of distinct letters in s_left and s_right is the same. Return the number of good splits you can make in s.

examples.explanation: There are 5 possible splits: ("a", "acaba"), ("aa", "caba"), ("aac", "aba"), ("aaca", "ba"), ("aacab", "a"). The good splits are ("aac", "aba") and ("aaca", "ba") which both have 2 distinct characters on both sides.

constraints: s consists of only lowercase English letters.

title: Check if Grid can be Cut into Sections
description: You are given an integer n representing the dimensions of an n x n grid, and a 2D integer array rectangles where rectangles[i] = [start_x, start_y, end_x, end_y] represents the coordinates of the bottom-left and top-right corners of a rectangle. Determine whether it is possible to make either two horizontal or two vertical cuts across the grid such that each cut divides the grid into non-empty sections and no rectangle is cut into two pieces.

examples.explanation: Two horizontal cuts can be made without slicing through any rectangle.

title: Rank Scores
description: Write a solution to find the rank of the scores. If there is a tie between two scores, both should have the same ranking. After a tie, the next ranking number should be the next consecutive integer (dense ranking). Return the result table ordered by score in descending order.

examples.explanation: Scores ranked densely from highest to lowest.

constraints: id is the primary key for the Scores table.
score is a numeric value with two decimal places.

title: Last Moment Before All Ants Fall Out of a Plank
description: We have a wooden plank of the length n units. Some ants are walking to the left, and other ants are walking to the right at 1 unit per second. When two ants moving in opposite directions meet, they immediately turn around and keep walking in the opposite direction. Finding the moment when the last ant(s) fall out of the plank is equivalent to assuming ants pass through each other without changing speed or direction.

examples.explanation: Ant at 4 moving left takes 4 seconds, ant at 0 moving right takes 4 seconds.

constraints: All values of left and right are unique.

title: Minimum Deletions to Make String Balanced
description: You are given a string s consisting only of characters 'a' and 'b'. You can delete any number of characters in s to make s balanced. s is balanced if there is no pair of indices (i, j) such that i < j and s[i] = 'b' and s[j]= 'a'. Return the minimum number of deletions needed to make s balanced.

examples.explanation: Delete the characters at index 2 and index 6 to result in "aaabbb".

title: Minimum Path Cost in a Grid
description: You are given a 0-indexed m x n integer matrix grid consisting of distinct integers from 0 to m * n - 1. You can move from a cell in row i to any cell in row i + 1. The cost of moving between cells is specified in a 2D integer array moveCost where moveCost[val][j] is the cost of moving from a cell of value val to the jth column of the next row. Return the minimum cost of a path that starts from any cell in the first row and ends at any cell in the last row.

examples.explanation: The path 5 -> 0 -> 1 has a total cost of 5 + (cost 5->0 = 3) + 0 + (cost 0->1 = 8) + 1 = 17.

constraints: grid consists of distinct integers from 0 to m * n - 1.

title: Corporate Flight Bookings
description: There are n flights that are labeled from 1 to n. You are given an array of flight bookings bookings, where bookings[i] = [first_i, last_i, seats_i] represents a booking for flights first_i through last_i (inclusive) with seats_i seats reserved for each flight in that range. Return an array answer of length n, where answer[i] is the total number of seats reserved for flight i.

examples.explanation: Flight 1: 10 seats, Flight 2: 10+20+25 = 55 seats, Flight 3: 20+25 = 45 seats, Flight 4: 25 seats, Flight 5: 25 seats.

title: All Nodes Distance K in Binary Tree
description: Given the root of a binary tree, the value of a target node target, and an integer k, return an array of the values of all nodes that have a distance k from the target node in the tree. You can return the answer in any order.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 500].
target is the value of one of the nodes in the tree.

Return the maximum number of boxes you can put into the warehouse.

examples.explanation: We can put box 1 into room 4, box 3 into room 1, and box 4 into room 0.

title: Maximum Matrix Sum
description: You are given an n x n integer matrix. You can do the following operation any number of times: choose any two adjacent cells of matrix and multiply each of their values by -1. Return the maximum summation of the matrix's elements using this operation.

examples.explanation: Multiply both negative numbers by -1 to make every element in the matrix positive, resulting in sum 4.

title: Populating Next Right Pointers in Each Node
description: You are given a perfect binary tree where all leaves are on the same level, and every parent has two children. Populate each next pointer to point to its next right node. If there is no next right node, the next pointer should be set to NULL. Initially, all next pointers are set to NULL.

examples.explanation: Nodes at each depth level are linked from left to right using their next pointers.

title: Throne Inheritance
description: A kingdom has a monarch and an inheritance succession system based on preorder traversal of family trees. Implement the ThroneInheritance class: ThroneInheritance(kingName) initializes the system with the king, birth(parentName, childName) records a new child, death(name) marks a person as deceased, and getInheritanceOrder() returns a list representing the current order of succession excluding dead people.

examples.output: [null, null, null, null, null, null, null, ["king", "andy", "matthew", "bob", "alex", "asha", "catherine"], null, ["king", "andy", "matthew", "alex", "asha", "catherine"]]
examples.explanation: Succession order generated dynamically based on preorder family relations.

At most 10^5 calls will be made in total to birth, death, and getInheritanceOrder.

description: You are given an m x n 0-indexed binary matrix grid. In one operation, you can choose any cell (row, col) containing a 1, and set all elements in that row and that column to 0. Return the minimum number of operations required to remove all 1's from the matrix.

examples.explanation: Select cell (0, 0) to clear row 0 and column 0, then select (1, 1) to clear remaining ones. Total 2 operations.

description: A set of real numbers can be represented as the union of intervals. You are given a sorted list of disjoint intervals intervals where intervals[i] = [a_i, b_i] representing the interval [a_i, b_i). You are also given an interval toBeRemoved = [c, d]. Return the set of intervals after removing every real number in toBeRemoved from intervals.

examples.explanation: Removing [1, 6) from intervals results in disjoint segments [[0,1], [6,7]].

constraints: intervals is sorted in ascending order with no overlapping segments.

description: Given two 1D vectors v1 and v2, implement an iterator to return their elements alternately. Implement the ZigzagIterator class with next() and hasNext() methods.

examples.explanation: Elements are taken alternately: 1 from v1, 3 from v2, 2 from v1, 4 from v2, followed by remaining elements 5 and 6 from v2.

title: Maximum Number of Operations to Move Ones to the End
description: You are given a binary string s. You can perform an operation where you pick an index i such that s[i] == '1' and s[i+1] == '0', and move this '1' (along with any adjacent '1's directly preceding it) to the right across contiguous zeros. Return the maximum number of operations you can perform.

examples.explanation: Pushing groups of ones to the rightmost zero blocks yields 4 total operations.

title: Find the Largest Area of Square Inside Two Rectangles
description: There exist n rectangles on a 2D plane. You are given two 2D integer arrays bottomLeft and topRight, each of size n x 2, where bottomLeft[i] = [a_i, b_i] and topRight[i] = [c_i, d_i] represent the bottom-left and top-right coordinates of the ith rectangle. Return the maximum area of a square that can fit inside the intersection of at least two rectangles. If no such square exists, return 0.

examples.explanation: The maximum intersection region between any pair of rectangles can enclose a square of area 1.

title: Convert Sorted List to Binary Search Tree
description: Given the head of a singly linked list where elements are sorted in ascending order, convert it to a height-balanced binary search tree.

examples.explanation: The output corresponds to a height-balanced BST built from the sorted list.

constraints: The number of nodes in head is in the range [0, 2 * 10^4].

title: Brace Expansion
description: You are given a string s representing a list of words. Each letter in the word has one or more options. If there are multiple options, the options are enclosed in curly braces, separated by commas (e.g., "{a,b,c}"). Return all words that can be formed in this manner, in lexicographical order.

examples.explanation: Expanding all combinations of choices across the curly braces in sorted order.

constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters, '{', '}', and ','.
s is guaranteed to be a valid expression.

title: Find Permutation
description: A permutation of the integers [1, 2, ..., n] can be represented as a signature string of length n - 1 with characters 'I' (Increase) and 'D' (Decrease). Given a string s containing only 'I' and 'D', construct and return the lexicographically smallest permutation that satisfies the given signature.

examples.explanation: [1,2] strictly increases matching "I".
[2,1,3] decreases from 2 to 1 and increases from 1 to 3.

title: Number of Wonderful Substrings
description: A wonderful string is a string where at most one letter appears an odd number of times. Given a string word consisting of first ten lowercase English letters ('a' through 'j'), return the number of wonderful non-empty substrings in word.

examples.explanation: The 4 wonderful substrings are "a" at 0, "b" at 1, "a" at 2, and "aba" across 0..2.

constraints: word consists of lowercase English letters from 'a' to 'j'.

title: Maximum Score From Removing Substrings
description: You are given a string s and two integers x and y. You can perform two types of operations: remove substring "ab" and gain x points, or remove substring "ba" and gain y points. Return the maximum points you can gain after applying the operations on s.

examples.explanation: Prioritize removing "ba" for 5 points, then remove remaining "ab" for 4 points.

constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Find the Smallest Divisor Given a Threshold
description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer threshold, we will choose a positive integer divisor, divide all the array by it, and sum the division's result (each result rounded up to the nearest integer). Find the smallest divisor such that the result mentioned above is less than or equal to threshold.

title: Put Boxes Into the Warehouse II
description: You are given two arrays of positive integers, boxes and warehouse. Unlike the previous variation, you can push boxes into the warehouse from both the left side and the right side. Return the maximum number of boxes you can put into the warehouse.

examples.explanation: We can push boxes from both ends to maximize warehouse storage.

description: Given two strings word1 and word2, return the minimum number of steps required to make word1 and word2 the same. In one step, you can delete exactly one character in either string.

examples.explanation: Delete 's' from "sea" to get "ea", and delete 't' from "eat" to get "ea".

constraints: word1 and word2 consist of only lowercase English letters.

title: Reordered Power of 2
description: You are given an integer n. We reorder the digits in any order (including the original order) such that the leading digit is not zero. Return true if and only if we can do this so that the resulting number is a power of two.

examples.explanation: 1 is already 2^0.
10 reordered can form 10 or 01, neither of which is a power of two without leading zero.
46 reordered becomes 64 which is 2^6.

description: You are given a nested list of integers nestedList. Each element is either an integer, or a list whose elements may also be integers or other lists. Implement an iterator to flatten it. Implement the NestedIterator class with next() returning the next integer, and hasNext() returning true if there are still some integers.

examples.explanation: Iterating sequentially through the flattened nested list.

title: Longest Palindromic Subsequence
description: Given a string s, find the longest palindromic subsequence's length in s. A subsequence is a sequence that can be derived from another sequence by deleting some or no elements without changing the order of the remaining elements.

examples.explanation: One possible longest palindromic subsequence is "bbbb".
One possible longest palindromic subsequence is "bb".

title: Camelcase Matching
description: Given an array of strings queries and a string pattern, return a boolean array answer where answer[i] is true if queries[i] matches pattern, and false otherwise. A query word matches pattern if you can insert lowercase letters into pattern so that it equals the query.

constraints: queries[i] and pattern consist of English letters.

title: Path with Maximum Probability
description: You are given an undirected weighted graph of n nodes (0-indexed), represented by an edge list where edges[i] = [a, b] is an undirected edge connecting the nodes a and b with a probability of success of traversing that edge succProb[i]. description: You are given a 0-indexed binary array nums of length n. nums can be divided at index i into two subarrays: nums_left and nums_right.
