examples.explanation: Division scores: at 0: 1, at 1: 2, at 2: 3, at 3: 2, at 4: 3. The maximum division score is 3 at indices 2 and 4.

title: Maximum Side Length of a Square with Sum Less than or Equal to Threshold
description: Given a m x n matrix mat and an integer threshold, return the maximum side-length of a square with a sum less than or equal to threshold or return 0 if there is no such square.

examples.explanation: The maximum side-length of square with sum <= 4 is 2 (e.g., top-left 2x2 submatrix with sum 4).

title: Complete Binary Tree Inserter
description: A complete binary tree is a binary tree in which every level, except possibly the last, is completely filled, and all nodes are as far left as possible. Implement the CBTInserter class: CBTInserter(root) initializes the data structure with the root of the tree, insert(val) inserts a TreeNode into the tree with value val to keep the tree complete, and returns the value of the parent of the inserted node, and get_root() returns the root node of the tree.

examples.explanation: CBTInserter initialized with root [1,2]. Inserting 3 attaches it to node 1. Inserting 4 attaches it to node 2.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree will be in the range [1, 1000].
root is a complete binary tree.
At most 10^4 calls will be made to insert and get_root.

title: Search Suggestions System
description: You are given an array of strings products and a string searchWord. Design a system that suggests at most three product names from products after each character of searchWord is typed. Suggested products should have common prefix with searchWord. If there are more than three products with a common prefix, return the three lexicographically minimums products. Return a list of lists of the suggested products after each character of searchWord is typed.

examples.explanation: Suggestions provided after typing each character: 'm', 'mo', 'mou', 'mous', 'mouse'.

constraints: All the strings of products are unique.
products[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
searchWord consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph
description: You have a graph of n nodes. You are given an integer n and an array edges where edges[i] = [a_i, b_i] indicates that there is an edge between a_i and b_i in the graph. Return the number of connected components in the graph.

examples.explanation: Component 1: {0, 1, 2}, Component 2: {3, 4}.
All vertices form a single connected component.

title: Find the Minimum Number of Fibonacci Numbers Whose Sum Is K
description: Given an integer k, return the minimum number of Fibonacci numbers whose sum is equal to k. The same Fibonacci number can be used multiple times. The Fibonacci numbers are defined as: F_1 = 1, F_2 = 1, F_n = F_{n-1} + F_{n-2} for n > 2.

examples.explanation: The Fibonacci numbers are: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ... For k = 7 we can use 2 + 5 = 7.
For k = 10 we can use 2 + 8 = 10.

title: Beautiful Arrangement
description: Suppose you have n integers labeled 1 through n. A permutation of these n integers perm (1-indexed) is considered a beautiful arrangement if for every i (1 <= i <= n), either perm[i] is divisible by i or i is divisible by perm[i]. Given an integer n, return the number of the beautiful arrangements that you can construct.

examples.explanation: The first beautiful arrangement is [1,2]: perm[1]=1 is divisible by 1, perm[2]=2 is divisible by 2. The second is [2,1]: perm[1]=2 is divisible by 1, 2 is divisible by perm[2]=1.
Only [1] can be formed.

title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
description: Given an n x n matrix where each of the rows and columns is sorted in ascending order, return the kth smallest element in the matrix. Note that it is the kth smallest element in the sorted order, not the kth distinct element. You must find a solution with a memory complexity better than O(n^2).

examples.explanation: The elements in the matrix are [1,5,9,10,11,12,13,13,15], and the 8th smallest number is 13.
The only element is -5.

constraints: All rows and columns of matrix are sorted in non-decreasing order.

title: Longest Nice Subarray
description: You are given an array nums consisting of positive integers. We call a subarray of nums nice if the bitwise AND of every pair of elements that are in different positions in the subarray is equal to 0. Return the length of the longest nice subarray.

examples.explanation: The longest nice subarray is [3,8,48]. 3 AND 8 = 0, 3 AND 48 = 0, 8 AND 48 = 0. Its length is 3.
The length of the longest nice subarray is 1.

title: House Robber IV
description: There are several consecutive houses along a street, each of which has some money inside. There is a robber who wants to steal money from the homes, but he cannot steal two adjacent houses. The capability of the robber is the maximum amount of money he steals from one house of all the houses he robbed. You are given an integer array nums representing how much money each house has and an integer k representing the minimum number of houses the robber must steal from. Return the minimum capability of the robber.

examples.explanation: Rob houses 0 and 2 with money [2, 5]. Maximum stolen value is 5.
Rob houses 0 and 3 with money [2, 3]. Maximum stolen value is 3.

title: Largest Values From Labels
description: You are given n item values and labels represented by two integer arrays values and labels. You are also given two integers numWanted and useLimit. Choose a subset of items s such that the size of the subset is at most numWanted, the number of items with the same label in s is at most useLimit, and the sum of values of the items in s is maximized. Return the maximum score of the subset.

examples.explanation: The subset chosen is the first, third, and fifth items with values [5, 3, 1] and labels [1, 2, 3]. Sum = 9.

title: Maximum Erasure Value
description: You are given an array of positive integers nums and want to erase a subarray containing unique elements. The score you get by erasing the subarray is equal to the sum of its elements. Return the maximum score you can get by erasing exactly one subarray.

examples.explanation: The optimal subarray here is [2,4,5,6] with score 17.
The optimal subarray is [5,2,1] or [1,2,5] with sum 8.

title: Find Kth Largest XOR Coordinate Value
description: You are given a 2D matrix of size m x n, consisting of non-negative integers. The coordinate value of (a, b) is the XOR sum of all matrix[i][j] where 0 <= i <= a < m and 0 <= j <= b < n (0-indexed). Find the kth largest value (1-indexed) of all the coordinate values of matrix.

examples.explanation: The coordinate values are: (0,0)->5, (0,1)->5^2=7, (1,0)->5^1=4, (1,1)->5^2^1^6=0. The largest value is 7.
The 2nd largest coordinate value is 5.

title: Max Chunks To Make Sorted
description: You are given an integer array arr of length n that represents a permutation of the integers in the range [0, n - 1]. We split arr into some number of chunks (i.e., partitions), and individually sort each chunk. After concatenating them, the result should equal the sorted array. Return the largest number of chunks we can make to sort the array.

examples.explanation: Splitting into two or more chunks will not return the required sorted array.
We can split into two chunks, such as [1, 0], [2, 3, 4]. Maximum number of chunks is 4: [1, 0], [2], [3], [4].

constraints: All the elements of arr are unique.

title: Walls and Gates
description: You are given an m x n grid rooms initialized with these three possible values: -1 represents a wall or an obstacle, 0 represents a gate, and 2147483647 (INF) represents an empty room. Fill each empty room with the distance to its nearest gate. If it is impossible to reach a gate, it should be filled with INF.

examples.explanation: Empty rooms are filled with the shortest distance to a gate.

title: Rotated Digits
description: An integer x is a good number if after rotating each digit individually by 180 degrees, we get a valid number that is different from x. Each digit must be rotated - 0, 1, and 8 rotate to themselves; 2 and 5 rotate to each other; 6 and 9 rotate to each other; all other numbers are invalid. Given an integer n, return the number of good integers in the range [1, n].

examples.explanation: There are four good numbers in the range [1, 10] : 2, 5, 6, 9. 1, 8, and 10 rotate into valid numbers but they equal themselves.

title: Image Overlap
description: You are given two images, img1 and img2, represented as binary, square matrices of size n x n. We translate one image however we choose by sliding it left, right, up, or down any number of units. After applying any translation, an overlap is the number of positions that have a 1 in both images. Return the largest possible overlap.

examples.explanation: Translate img1 right by 1 unit and down by 1 unit to maximize overlap to 3.
Both images overlap at position (0,0).

title: Escape The Ghosts
description: You are playing a simplified PAC-MAN game on an infinite 2D grid. You start at the point [0, 0] and are trying to get to the destination point [target_x, target_y]. There are several ghosts on the grid with coordinates ghosts[i] = [g_x, g_y]. Each turn, you and all ghosts may move 1 unit in any of the 4 cardinal directions. You escape if and only if you can reach the target before any ghost can reach you or the target. Return true if you can escape, or false otherwise.

examples.explanation: You can reach destination [0, 1] in 1 step without any ghost intercepting you.
The ghost can reach target [2, 0] at the same time or before you.

title: Count Pairs of Equal Substrings With Minimum Difference
description: You are given two strings firstString and secondString consisting of lowercase English letters. Count the number of quadruplets (i, j, a, b) such that: firstString[i...j] == secondString[a...b] (a non-empty common substring of length 1), and the value j - a is minimized among all valid pairs. Return the total count of such quadruplets with the minimum difference j - a.

examples.explanation: The pair with smallest j - a is chosen by taking 'a' at index 0 in firstString and index 4 in secondString, or 'c' / 'd' correspondingly.

constraints: firstString and secondString consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Two Best Non-Overlapping Events
description: You are given a 2D integer array events where events[i] = [startTime_i, endTime_i, value_i]. You can choose at most two non-overlapping events to attend such that the sum of their values is maximized. If you attend an event that ends at time t, the next event must start at time >= t + 1. Return the maximum sum of values.

examples.explanation: Choose event 0 (value 2) and event 1 (value 2) for maximum sum 4.
Choose event 2 with value 5.

title: Find the Number of Ways to Place People I
description: You are given a 2D array points where points[i] = [x_i, y_i] represents the coordinates of the ith person. Return the number of pairs of people (A, B) such that person A is to the upper-left of person B (x_A <= x_B and y_A >= y_B) and no other person is located strictly inside or on the boundary of the rectangular region formed by A and B.

examples.explanation: There are no valid pairs where the first is upper-left of the second.

title: Unique Binary Search Trees
description: Given an integer n, return the number of structurally unique BST's (binary search trees) which has exactly n nodes of unique values from 1 to n.

examples.explanation: There are 5 structurally unique binary search trees with 3 nodes.
Only 1 unique BST exists for n = 1.

title: Binary Searchable Numbers in an Unsorted Array
description: Consider a standard binary search algorithm on an unsorted array nums. An element nums[i] is binary searchable if and only if the binary search procedure is guaranteed to locate it regardless of the pivot selections. Return the number of binary searchable elements in nums.

examples.explanation: Single-element array is always binary searchable.
Only -1 is guaranteed to be found regardless of pivot choice.

constraints: All values of nums are unique.

title: Permutations II
description: Given a collection of numbers, nums, that might contain duplicates, return all possible unique permutations in any order.

examples.explanation: All unique permutations containing duplicates.
All 6 permutations of unique values.

title: Smallest Subsequence of Distinct Characters
description: Given a string s, return the lexicographically smallest subsequence of s that contains all the distinct characters of s exactly once.

examples.explanation: "abc" contains distinct characters and is lexicographically smallest.
"acdb" is the smallest valid subsequence.

constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Find All Lonely Numbers in the Array
description: You are given an integer array nums. A number x is lonely when it appears only once, and no adjacent numbers (x + 1 and x - 1) appear in the array. Return all lonely numbers in nums in any order.

examples.explanation: 10 is lonely (10 occurs once, 9 and 11 not in array). 8 is lonely (8 occurs once, 7 and 9 not in array). 6 and 5 are adjacent, so neither is lonely.

title: Compare Strings by Frequency of the Smallest Character
description: Let f(s) be the frequency of the lexicographically smallest character in a non-empty string s. Given arrays of strings queries and words, return an integer array answer where answer[i] is the number of words such that f(queries[i]) < f(W) for word W in words.

examples.explanation: f("cbd") = 1 ('b'), f("zaaaz") = 3 ('a'). 1 < 3, so answer is [1].
f("bbb") = 3, matches "aaaa" (4). f("cc") = 2, matches "aaa" (3) and "aaaa" (4).

constraints: queries[i][j], words[i][j] consist of lowercase English letters.

title: My Calendar II
description: You are implementing a program to use as your calendar. We can add a new event if adding the event will not cause a triple booking. A triple booking happens when three events have some non-empty intersection. Implement the MyCalendarTwo class with a book(startTime, endTime) method that returns true if the event can be added without creating a triple booking, or false otherwise.

examples.output: [null, true, true, true, false, true, true]
examples.explanation: Booking [5, 15] is rejected because it overlaps with [10, 20] and [10, 40], creating a triple booking.

constraints: At most 1000 calls will be made to book.

title: Longest String Chain
description: You are given an array of words where each word consists of lowercase English letters. wordA is a predecessor of wordB if and only if we can insert exactly one letter anywhere in wordA without changing the order of the other characters to make it equal to wordB. Return the length of the longest possible word chain with words chosen from the given list of words.

examples.explanation: One of the longest word chains is ["a","ba","bda","bdca"].
All 5 words can form the chain ["xb", "xbc", "cxbc", "pcxbc", "pcxbcf"].

constraints: words[i] only consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Most Stones Removed with Same Row or Column
description: On a 2D plane, we place n stones at some integer coordinate points. Each coordinate point may have at most one stone. A stone can be removed if it shares either the same row or the same column as another stone that has not been removed. Given an array stones of length n where stones[i] = [x_i, y_i], return the largest possible number of stones that can be removed.

examples.explanation: 5 stones can be removed by following connected components.
3 stones can be removed.

constraints: No two stones are at the same coordinate point.

title: Flatten a Multilevel Doubly Linked List
description: You are given a doubly linked list, which contains nodes that have a next pointer, a previous pointer, and an additional child pointer. This child pointer may or may not point to a separate doubly linked list, also containing these special nodes. Flatten the list so that all the nodes appear in a single-level, doubly linked list in preorder traversal.

examples.explanation: The multilevel doubly linked list is flattened by following child lists recursively.

constraints: The number of Nodes will not exceed 1000.

title: Count Positions on Street With Required Brightness
description: You are given an integer n. A street is represented by a number line starting at position 0 and ending at position n - 1. You are also given a 2D integer array lights where lights[i] = [position_i, range_i] indicates that there is a street light at position position_i with a reach of range_i. Finally, you are given a 0-indexed integer array requirement of size n where requirement[j] is the minimum brightness needed at position j. Return the number of positions on the street that meet the requirement.

examples.explanation: Positions 0, 1, 2, and 4 receive brightness greater than or equal to their requirement.

title: Push Dominoes
description: There are n dominoes in a line, and we place each domino vertically upright. In the beginning, we simultaneously push some of the dominoes either to the left or to the right. After each second, each domino falling to the left pushes the adjacent domino on the left, and similarly for the right. When a vertical domino has dominoes falling on it from both sides, it stays still due to the balance of forces. Given a string dominoes representing the initial state, return a string representing the final state.

examples.explanation: The first domino expends no force on the second, and the third remains vertical due to opposing forces.
Forces propagate outwards until all dominoes stabilize.

title: Product of the Last K Numbers
description: Design an algorithm that accepts a stream of integers and retrieves the product of the last k integers of the stream. Implement the ProductOfNumbers class: ProductOfNumbers() initializes the object with an empty stream, add(num) appends the integer num to the stream, and getProduct(k) returns the product of the last k numbers in the current list in O(1) time.

examples.explanation: getProduct(2) returns 5 * 4 = 20, getProduct(3) returns 2 * 5 * 4 = 40, getProduct(4) returns 0.

constraints: At most 4 * 10^4 calls will be made to add and getProduct.

title: Range Sum of Sorted Subarray Sums
description: You are given the array nums consisting of n positive integers. You computed the sum of all non-empty continuous subarrays, sorted them in non-decreasing order, creating a new array of n * (n + 1) / 2 numbers. Return the sum of the numbers from index left to index right (1-indexed) modulo 10^9 + 7.

examples.explanation: All subarray sums are 1, 3, 6, 10, 2, 5, 9, 3, 7, 4. Sorted: [1, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10]. Sum from index 1 to 5 is 1 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 4 = 13.

title: Unique Binary Search Trees II
description: Given an integer n, return all the structurally unique BST's (binary search trees), which has exactly n nodes of unique values from 1 to n. Return the answer in any order.

examples.explanation: All 5 structurally unique binary search trees built using nodes 1, 2, and 3.

title: Add Two Numbers II
description: You are given two non-empty linked lists representing two non-negative integers. The most significant digit comes first and each of their nodes contains a single digit. Add the two numbers and return the sum as a linked list. You may assume the two numbers do not contain any leading zero, except the number 0 itself.
constraints: The number of nodes in each linked list is in the range [1, 100].
It is guaranteed that the list represents a number that does not have leading zeros.

title: The k Strongest Values in an Array
description: Given an array of integers arr and an integer k. An element arr[i] is stronger than arr[j] if |arr[i] - m| > |arr[j] - m| where m is the median of the array. If |arr[i] - m| == |arr[j] - m|, arr[i] is stronger than arr[j] if arr[i] > arr[j]. Return a list of the strongest k values in the array in any order.

examples.explanation: Median is 3. |5-3|=2 and |1-3|=2. 5 and 1 are the strongest values.

title: Lonely Pixel I
description: Given an m x n picture consisting of black 'B' and white 'W' pixels, return the number of black lonely pixels. A black lonely pixel is 'B' that is located at a position where no other black pixels are in the same row and column.

examples.explanation: All three 'B' pixels are lonely since each is unique in its row and column.

title: Best Sightseeing Pair
description: You are given an integer array values where values[i] represents the value of the ith sightseeing spot. Two sightseeing spots i and j have a score equal to values[i] + values[j] + i - j (where i < j). Return the maximum score of a pair of sightseeing spots.

examples.explanation: i = 0, j = 2, values[i] + values[j] + i - j = 8 + 5 + 0 - 2 = 11.

title: Find the Minimum Amount of Time to Brew Potions
description: You are given an integer array potions where potions[i] is the amount of potion required, and an array of brewing times. Calculate the minimum amount of time needed to brew all required potions under standard capacity constraints.

examples.explanation: The optimal allocation of brewing operations minimizes overall completion time.

title: Minimum Time Difference
description: Given a list of 24-hour clock time points in "HH:MM" format, return the minimum minutes difference between any two time-points in the list.

examples.explanation: The minimum time difference is 1 minute.
Identical time points yield 0 minutes difference.

title: Path Sum II
description: Given the root of a binary tree and an integer targetSum, return all root-to-leaf paths where the sum of the node values in the path equals targetSum. Each path should be returned as a list of the node values, not node references.

examples.explanation: There are two paths whose sum equals targetSum: 5 + 4 + 11 + 2 = 22, and 5 + 8 + 4 + 5 = 22.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 5000].

title: Integer Break
description: Given an integer n, break it into the sum of k positive integers, where k >= 2, and maximize the product of those integers. Return the maximum product you can get.

title: Number of Equal Numbers Blocks
description: You are given a 0-indexed integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order. An equal numbers block is a maximal contiguous subarray of nums where all elements are equal. Return the total number of equal numbers blocks in nums using binary search techniques.

examples.explanation: The distinct contiguous equal blocks are [1,1], [2,2], and [3,3,3].

constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order.

title: Frog Jump II
description: You are given a 0-indexed integer array stones sorted in strictly increasing order representing the positions of stones in a river. A frog, initially on the first stone, wants to travel to the last stone and then return to the first stone by jumping from stone to stone. The length of a jump is the absolute difference between the positions of the stones. Each stone can be visited at most once, except the first and last stones. Return the minimum maximum jump length of the frog.

examples.explanation: The frog can jump forward [0, 5, 7] and backward [7, 6, 2, 0]. The maximum jump distance is 5.

title: Parallel Courses
description: You are given an integer n, which indicates that there are n courses labeled from 1 to n. You are also given an array relations where relations[i] = [prevCourse_i, nextCourse_i], representing a prerequisite relationship. In one semester, you can take any number of courses as long as you have taken all their prerequisites in previous semesters. Return the minimum number of semesters needed to take all courses. If there is no way to take all the courses, return -1.

examples.explanation: In semester 1, courses 1 and 2 are taken. In semester 2, course 3 is taken.

title: All Ancestors of a Node in a Directed Acyclic Graph
description: You are given a positive integer n representing the number of nodes of a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG), numbered from 0 to n - 1 (inclusive). You are also given a 2D integer array edges, where edges[i] = [from_i, to_i] denotes a directed edge. Return a list answer, where answer[i] is the list of ancestors of the ith node, sorted in ascending order.

examples.explanation: The ancestors of node 3 are [0, 1]. The ancestors of node 4 are [0, 2].

title: Find the Length of the Longest Common Prefix
description: You are given two arrays with positive integers arr1 and arr2. A prefix of a positive integer is an integer formed by one or more of its digits starting from its leftmost digit. Return the length of the longest common prefix between all pairs of integers (x, y) such that x belongs to arr1 and y belongs to arr2. If no common prefix exists, return 0.

examples.explanation: The longest common prefix between 100 and 1000 is "100", which has a length of 3.

title: Confirmation Rate
description: The confirmation rate of a user is the number of 'confirmed' messages divided by the total number of requested confirmation messages. The confirmation rate of a user that did not request any confirmation messages is 0. Round the confirmation rate to two decimal places. Write a solution to find the confirmation rate of each user.

examples.explanation: Calculates success percentage across all signup accounts.

constraints: user_id is the unique identifier in Signups.
action is an ENUM of type ('confirmed', 'timeout').

title: Maximum Font to Fit a Sentence in a Screen
description: You are given a string text. We want to display text on a screen of width w and height h. You can choose any font size from an array fonts, which is sorted in increasing order. You have a FontInfo API that gives the width and height of any character under a given font size. Return the maximum font size from fonts that can be used so that the entire text fits on the screen on a single line, or -1 if no font size fits.

examples.explanation: Font size 6 is the largest font size that fits text within the bounds.

constraints: text consists of lowercase English letters.
fonts is sorted in strictly increasing order.

title: Boats to Save People
description: You are given an array people where people[i] is the weight of the ith person, and an infinite number of boats where each boat can carry a maximum weight of limit. Each boat carries at most two people at the same time, provided the sum of the weight of those people is at most limit. Return the minimum number of boats to carry every given person.

examples.explanation: 1 boat with weight (1, 2).
3 boats with weights (1, 2), (2), and (3).
4 boats with weights (3), (3), (4), (5).

title: Knight Dialer
description: The chess knight has a unique movement: it may move two squares vertically and one square horizontally, or two squares horizontally and one square vertically. You have a standard phone keypad placing digits 0-9. We place a chess knight on any numeric cell, and the knight makes n - 1 hops to generate a phone number of length n. Return how many distinct phone numbers of length n you can dial modulo 10^9 + 7.

examples.explanation: We need to dial a number of length 1, so placing the knight over any digit yields 10 numbers.
All valid 2-digit phone numbers reachable by one knight move.
Compute count modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Flip String to Monotone Increasing
description: A binary string is monotone increasing if it consists of some number of 0's (possibly none), followed by some number of 1's (also possibly none). You are given a binary string s. You can flip s[i] changing it from 0 to 1 or from 1 to 0. Return the minimum number of flips to make s monotone increasing.

examples.explanation: We flip the last digit to get 00111.
We flip to get 011111, or 000111.

title: Minimum Cost Path with Edge Reversals
description: You are given a directed graph with n nodes labeled 0 to n - 1 and an array of directed edges. You want to find the minimum cost to travel from a start node to a target node, where reversing the direction of an edge incurs a specific additional cost. Return the minimum cost required.

examples.explanation: Reversing the edge [2,1] to [1,2] allows a valid path 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 with 1 reversal.

title: Peeking Iterator
description: Design an iterator that supports the peek operation on an existing iterator in addition to the hasNext and the next operations. Implement the PeekingIterator class: PeekingIterator(Iterator<int> nums) initializes the object with the given iterator, peek() returns the next element in the array without advancing the iterator, next() returns the next element in the array and moves the pointer forward, and hasNext() returns true if there are still elements in the array.

examples.explanation: Peeking returns 2 without consuming it; subsequent next() returns 2.

constraints: All calls to next and peek are valid.

title: Shortest Way to Form String
description: A subsequence of a string is a new string that is formed from the original string by deleting some (can be none) of the characters without disturbing the relative positions of the remaining characters. Given two strings source and target, return the minimum number of subsequences of source such that their concatenation equals target. If the task is impossible, return -1.

examples.explanation: Target "abcbc" can be formed by "abc" and "bc", which are both subsequences of source.
Target cannot be formed because character 'd' is missing from source.

constraints: source and target consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Number of Same-End Substrings
description: You are given a 0-indexed string s and a 2D integer array queries where queries[i] = [l_i, r_i]. For each query, return the number of same-end substrings in the substring s[l_i...r_i]. A same-end substring is a substring that starts and ends with the same character.

examples.explanation: In query [1,4] (substring "bcaa"), the same-end substrings are "b", "c", "a", "a", "aa" (total 5).

constraints: s consists only of lowercase English letters.

title: Check If a String Contains All Binary Codes of Size K
description: Given a binary string s and an integer k, return true if every binary code of length k is a substring of s. Otherwise, return false.

examples.explanation: The binary codes of length 2 are "00", "01", "10" and "11". They exist at indices 0, 1, 3, and 2 respectively.
Binary codes of length 1 are "0" and "1", both present in s.
Binary code "00" is not present in s.

title: Sum of Subarray Ranges
description: You are given an integer array nums. The range of a subarray of nums is the difference between the largest and smallest element in the subarray. Return the sum of all subarray ranges of nums.

examples.explanation: Sum of ranges across all contiguous subarrays is 4.

title: Maximum Product of Word Lengths
description: Given a string array words, return the maximum value of length(word[i]) * length(word[j]) where the two words do not share common letters. If no such two words exist, return 0.

examples.explanation: The two words can be "abcw", "xtfn" with product 4 * 4 = 16.
The two words can be "ab", "cd" with product 2 * 2 = 4.

constraints: words[i] consists only of lowercase English letters.

title: Smallest String Starting From Leaf
description: You are given the root of a binary tree where each node has a value in the range [0, 25] representing the lowercase English letters from a to z. Return the lexicographically smallest string that starts at a leaf of this tree and ends at the root. A leaf is a node with no children.

examples.explanation: The paths from leaf to root are "dba", "eba", "dba", and "eba". The smallest is "dba".
The smallest lexicographical leaf-to-root string is "adz".

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 8500].

title: Tree Diameter
description: The diameter of a tree is the number of edges in the longest path in that tree. There is an undirected tree of n nodes labeled 0 to n - 1. You are given a 2D array edges where edges[i] = [u, v] indicates that there is an undirected edge between nodes u and v. Return the diameter of the tree.

examples.explanation: The longest path of the tree is the path between node 1 and node 2, which has 2 edges.
The longest path is 3 -> 2 -> 1 -> 4 -> 5, with 4 edges.

title: Plus One Linked List
description: Given a non-negative integer represented as a singly linked list of digits, plus one to the integer. The digits are stored such that the most significant digit is at the head of the list.
constraints: The number of nodes in the linked list is in the range [1, 100].
The number represented does not have leading zeros except 0 itself.

title: Beautiful Arrangement II
description: Given two integers n and k, construct a list answer that contains n different positive integers from 1 to n and has exactly k distinct integers among the absolute differences of adjacent elements. Return the list answer. If there are multiple answers, return any of them.

examples.explanation: The [1,2,3] has three different positive integers, and absolute differences are [1, 1], which has exactly 1 distinct integer: 1.
The [1,3,2] has three different positive integers, and absolute differences are [2, 1], which has exactly 2 distinct integers: 1 and 2.

title: Minimum Falling Path Sum
description: Given an n x n array of integers matrix, return the minimum sum of any falling path through matrix. A falling path starts at any element in the first row and chooses the element in the next row that is either directly below or diagonally left/right.

examples.explanation: The falling path with the minimum sum is [1, 4, 8] with sum 13.
The falling path with minimum sum is [-19, -40] with sum -59.

title: Delete the Middle Node of a Linked List
description: You are given the head of a linked list. Delete the middle node, and return the head of the modified linked list. The middle node of a linked list of size n is the ⌊n / 2⌋th node from the 0-indexed beginning.

examples.explanation: Since n = 7, node 3 with value 7 is the middle node and is deleted.
Since n = 4, node 2 with value 3 is the middle node and is deleted.

constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [1, 10^5].

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make Word K-Periodic
description: You are given a string word of size n, and an integer k such that n is a multiple of k. In one operation, you can pick any two indices i and j that are multiples of k and replace the substring of length k starting at i with the substring of length k starting at j. Return the minimum number of operations required to make word k-periodic.

examples.explanation: We can replace the substring "code" with "leet" to get "leetleetleet", which is 4-periodic.
3 operations needed to make all 2-length blocks identical.

constraints: word consists only of lowercase English letters.

title: People Whose List of Favorite Companies Is Not a Subset of Another List
description: Given the array favoriteCompanies where favoriteCompanies[i] is the list of favorite companies for the ith person (indexed from 0). Return the indices of people whose list of favorite companies is not a subset of any other list of favorite companies. You must return the indices in increasing order.

examples.explanation: Person 2's list is a subset of Person 0's list. Person 3's list is a subset of Person 0's and Person 2's lists.

constraints: All strings in favoriteCompanies[i] are distinct.
All lists of favorite companies are distinct.

title: Pyramid Transition Matrix
description: You are stacking blocks to form a pyramid. Each block has a color represented by a single letter. We are given the bottom row bottom and a list of allowed patterns allowed where allowed[i] = "ABC" means if the two adjacent blocks on a lower row are 'A' and 'B', the block directly above them can be 'C'. Return true if you can successfully build the pyramid to the top, or false otherwise.

examples.explanation: We can stack 'C' over 'BC' and 'E' over 'CD' to get row "CE", then stack 'A' over "CE" to finish the pyramid.
We cannot build the pyramid to the top.

constraints: All characters in bottom and allowed are uppercase English letters from 'A' to 'G'.

title: Generalized Abbreviation
description: A generalized abbreviation of a word can be generated by replacing any number of non-overlapping, non-adjacent substrings with their lengths. Given a string word, return a list of all the possible generalized abbreviations of word. Return the answer in any order.

examples.explanation: All 16 possible generalized abbreviations of "word".

constraints: word consists only of lowercase English letters.

title: The Maze
description: There is a ball in a maze with empty spaces (0) and walls (1). The ball can go through empty spaces by rolling up, down, left or right, but it won't stop rolling until hitting a wall. When the ball stops, it could choose the next direction. Given the m x n maze, the ball's start position and the destination, return true if the ball can stop at the destination, otherwise return false.

examples.explanation: One possible way is : left -> down -> left -> down -> right -> down -> right.
The ball cannot stop at the destination position.

title: Time Needed to Inform All Employees
description: A company has n employees with a unique ID from 0 to n - 1. The head of the company is headID. Each employee has one direct manager given in the manager array where manager[headID] = -1. When an employee i receives news, they need informTime[i] minutes to inform all their direct subordinates. Return the number of minutes needed to inform all employees about the news.

examples.explanation: The head of the company is the only employee in the company.
The head of the company with id = 2 informs all other employees in 1 minute.

constraints: informTime[i] == 0 if employee i has no subordinates.

title: Reschedule Meetings for Maximum Free Time II
description: You are given an integer eventTime denoting the duration of an event. You are also given two integer arrays startTime and endTime of length n representing the start and end times of n non-overlapping meetings. You can reschedule at most one meeting to another time interval of the same duration without overlapping other meetings. Return the maximum continuous free time you can obtain.

examples.explanation: Reschedule meeting [1, 2] to [2, 3] to get continuous free time from 0 to 2.
Reschedule meeting [0, 1] into [8, 9] to get continuous free time from 0 to 7.

title: Last Stone Weight II
description: You are given an array of integers stones where stones[i] is the weight of the ith stone. We play a game with the stones: on each turn, we choose any two stones with weights x and y (x <= y) and smash them together. If x == y, both stones are destroyed. If x != y, the stone of weight x is destroyed, and the stone of weight y has new weight y - x. At the end of the game, there is at most one stone left. Return the smallest possible weight of the left stone.

examples.explanation: We can combine 2 and 4 to get 2, then combine 7 and 8 to get 1, then combine 2 and 1 to get 1, then combine 1 and 1 to get 0, left with 1.
The minimal remaining weight is 5.

title: Solving Questions With Brainpower
description: You are given a 0-indexed 2D integer array questions where questions[i] = [points_i, brainpower_i]. You solve questions sequentially. If you solve question i, you earn points_i points, but you will be unable to solve each of the next brainpower_i questions. If you skip question i, you get 0 points and can make the next decision on question i + 1. Return the maximum points you can earn.

examples.explanation: Earn maximum points by solving questions 0 and 3: 3 + 2 = 5.
Solve question 1 (2 points) and question 4 (5 points): 2 + 5 = 7.

title: Rank Teams by Votes
description: In a special ranking system, each voter gives a rank from highest to lowest to all teams participating in the competition. The ordering of teams is decided by who received the most position-one votes. If two or more teams tie in the first position, we consider the second position to resolve the conflict, and so on. If they tie in all positions, sort them alphabetically. Return a string of teams sorted by the ranking system.

examples.explanation: Team A received 5 first place votes. Team C received 3 second place votes while Team B received 2 second place votes. Therefore, the order is "ACB".
'X' is sorted ahead of 'W' as a tie-breaker.

constraints: votes[i].length == votes[j].length for all i, j
votes[i] contains all uppercase English letters.

title: Sender With Largest Word Count
description: You have a chat log of messages. You are given two string arrays messages and senders where messages[i] is a message sent by senders[i]. A word is defined as a sequence of characters separated by a single space. Return the sender with the largest total word count. If there is more than one sender with the same word count, return the lexicographically largest name.

examples.input: messages = ["Hello userTwooo","Hi userThree","Wonderful day Alice","Nice day userThree"], senders = ["Alice","userTwo","userThree","Alice"]
examples.explanation: Alice sent two messages with a total of 2 + 3 = 5 words, which is the maximum.

constraints: messages[i] consists of uppercase and lowercase English letters and spaces.

title: Alternating Groups II
description: There is a circle of red and blue tiles. You are given an array of integers colors and an integer k. The tile colors are represented by colors[i], where 0 represents red and 1 represents blue. An alternating group is every k contiguous tiles in the circle with alternating colors. Return the number of alternating groups.

examples.explanation: The alternating groups of length 3 are [0,1,0] starting at index 0, [1,0,1] starting at index 1, and [0,1,0] starting at index 2.

title: Destroying Asteroids
description: You are given an integer mass, which represents the original mass of a planet. You are also given an integer array asteroids, where asteroids[i] is the mass of the ith asteroid. You can arrange for the planet to collide with the asteroids in any order. If the mass of the planet is greater than or equal to the mass of the asteroid, the asteroid is destroyed and the planet gains its mass. Otherwise, the planet is destroyed. Return true if all asteroids can be destroyed.

examples.explanation: One way to destroy all asteroids is: collide with 3 (mass becomes 13), collide with 5 (mass becomes 18), collide with 9 (mass becomes 27), collide with 19 (mass becomes 46), collide with 21 (mass becomes 67).

title: Maximum Split of Positive Even Integers
description: You are given an integer finalSum. Split it into a sum of a maximum number of unique positive even integers. Return a list of integers that represent a valid split. If no valid split exists, return an empty list.

examples.explanation: The maximum number of even integers is 3, with elements [2, 4, 6].
There is no valid split since 7 is odd.

title: Bag of Tokens
description: You start with an initial power of power, an initial score of 0, and a bag of tokens given as an integer array tokens. To maximize your score, you can play tokens face up (spend token power, gain 1 score if power >= token) or face down (spend 1 score, gain token power if score >= 1). Each token can be played at most once. Return the maximum score you can achieve.

examples.explanation: Play token 100 face up, power becomes 50, score becomes 1.
Play 100 face up (power = 100, score = 1), play 400 face down (power = 500, score = 0), play 200 face up (power = 300, score = 1), play 300 face up (power = 0, score = 2).

title: Is Graph Bipartite?
description: There is an undirected graph with n nodes, where each node is numbered between 0 and n - 1. You are given a 2D array graph, where graph[u] is an array of nodes that node u is adjacent to. Return true if and only if it is bipartite (nodes can be partitioned into two independent sets such that every edge connects a node in one set to a node in the other).

examples.explanation: There is no way to partition the nodes into two independent sets such that every edge connects nodes in different sets.
We can partition the nodes into two sets: {0, 2} and {1, 3}.

constraints: All values in graph[u] are unique.

title: Shortest Bridge
description: You are given an n x n binary matrix grid where 1 represents land and 0 represents water. An island is a 4-directionally connected group of 1s not connected to any other 1s. There are exactly two islands in grid. You may change 0's to 1's to connect the two islands to form one island. Return the smallest number of 0's you must flip to connect the two islands.

examples.explanation: Flip the 0 at (0, 0) or (1, 1) to connect the two islands.
Flipping two 0s connects the islands.

constraints: There are exactly two islands in grid.

title: Divide Array in Sets of K Consecutive Numbers
description: Given an array of integers nums and a positive integer k, check whether it is possible to divide this array into sets of k consecutive numbers. Return true if possible, or false otherwise.

examples.explanation: Array can be divided into [1,2,3,4] and [3,4,5,6].
Array can be divided into [1,2,3], [2,3,4], [3,4,5], and [9,10,11].

title: Minimum Time to Repair Cars
description: You are given an integer array ranks representing the ranks of some mechanics. ranks[i] is the rank of the ith mechanic. A mechanic with rank r can repair n cars in r * n^2 minutes. You are also given an integer cars representing the total number of cars waiting in the garage. Return the minimum time taken to repair all the cars when mechanics work simultaneously.

examples.explanation: Mechanic 0 repairs 2 cars (16 mins), Mechanic 1 repairs 2 cars (8 mins), Mechanic 2 repairs 2 cars (12 mins), Mechanic 3 repairs 4 cars (16 mins). Total time is 16.

title: RLE Iterator
description: We can use run-length encoding to write a sequence of integers. Given a run-length encoded array encoding, design an iterator that traverses the decoded elements. Implement the RLEIterator class: RLEIterator(int[] encoding) initializes the object with the run-length encoded array, and next(int n) exhausts the next n elements and returns the last element exhausted, or -1 if there are no more elements.

examples.explanation: Decoded array is [8,8,8,5,5]. Calling next(2) returns 8, next(1) returns 8, next(1) returns 5, next(2) exhausts elements and returns -1.

constraints: At most 1000 calls will be made to next.

title: Monthly Transactions I
description: Write an SQL query to find for each month and country, the number of transactions and their total amount, the number of approved transactions and their total amount. Return the result table in any order.

examples.input: Transactions table: [id, country, state, amount, trans_date]
examples.explanation: Aggregates transactions grouped by year-month and country.

constraints: id is the primary key of the table.
state is an ENUM of type ('approved', 'declined').

title: Partition String
description: Given a string s, partition the string into one or more non-empty substrings such that each character in s appears in at most one substring. Return the maximum number of substrings possible.

examples.explanation: Two possible valid partitions are ("a","ba","cab","a") and ("ab","a","ca","ba").

constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters.

title: Minimum Difference Between Largest and Smallest Value in Three Moves
description: You are given an integer array nums. In one move, you can choose one element of nums and change it to any value. Return the minimum difference between the largest and smallest value of nums after performing at most three moves.

examples.explanation: Change 2, 3, and 4 to 5 to make all elements 5. The difference is 5 - 5 = 0.
Change 0, 10, and 14 to 5 to get [1, 5, 5, 5, 5] with difference 5 - 1 = 1.

title: Campus Bikes
description: On a campus represented on the X-Y plane, there are n workers and m bikes, with n <= m. Each worker and bike is a 2D coordinate. Assign each worker to a bike based on Manhattan distance: pairs with the shortest distance are assigned first. Break ties by smallest worker index, then smallest bike index. Return an array of length n where result[i] is the index of the bike assigned to the ith worker.

examples.explanation: Worker 1 grabs Bike 0 first because distance is 1. Then Worker 0 grabs Bike 1.

title: Minimum Path Cost in a Hidden Grid
description: This is an interactive problem. There is a robot in a hidden grid trying to reach a target cell with minimum cost. The grid consists of empty cells and blocked cells. Each cell has an entry cost. The robot can move in 4 directions using the GridMaster API. Return the minimum total cost to reach the target cell, or -1 if unreachable.

examples.explanation: Robot moves right to (0,1) with cost 3, or down to (1,0) with cost 1 then right to (1,1) with cost 1. Minimum total cost is 1 + 1 = 2.

title: Adjacent Increasing Subarrays Detection II
description: Given an array of integers nums, find the maximum integer k such that there exist two adjacent contiguous subarrays of length k that are strictly increasing. Return the maximum possible value of k.

examples.explanation: The subarray [5,7,8] and [9,2,3] or [2,5,7] and [8,9,2] are valid candidates with maximum length 3.

title: Design Tic-Tac-Toe
description: Assume the following rules are for the Tic-Tac-Toe game on an n x n board: A move is guaranteed to be valid and is placed on an empty block. A player who places n of their marks in a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal row wins the game. Implement TicTacToe class: TicTacToe(int n) initializes the board of size n, and makeMove(int row, int col, int player) indicates that the player makes a move and returns 0 (no winner), 1 (player 1 wins), or 2 (player 2 wins).

examples.explanation: Player 1 wins on placing mark at (2, 1) completing the bottom row.

constraints: At most n^2 calls will be made to move.

title: Department Highest Salary
description: Write a solution to find employees who have the highest salary in each of the departments from Employee and Department tables. Return the result table in any order.

examples.input: Employee table: [id, name, salary, departmentId], Department table: [id, name]
examples.explanation: Finds maximum salary per departmentId matched with Department names.

constraints: id is the primary key for Employee and Department tables.
departmentId is a foreign key referencing Department.id.

title: Range Sum Query 2D - Immutable
description: Given a 2D matrix matrix, handle multiple queries of the following type: calculate the sum of the elements of matrix inside the rectangle defined by its upper left corner (row1, col1) and lower right corner (row2, col2). Implement NumMatrix class with sumRegion(int row1, int col1, int row2, int col2) in O(1) time.

examples.explanation: sumRegion(2, 1, 4, 3) calculates the submatrix sum as 8.

constraints: At most 10^4 calls will be made to sumRegion.

title: Binary String With Substrings Representing 1 To N
description: Given a binary string s and a positive integer n, return true if the binary representation of all the integers from 1 to n are substrings of s, or false otherwise.

examples.explanation: The binary representations of 1, 2, and 3 are "1", "10", and "11", which are all substrings of "0110".
4 in binary is "100", which is not a substring of "0110".

title: Maximum Beauty of an Array After Applying Operation
description: You are given a 0-indexed array nums and a non-negative integer k. In one operation, you can replace any element nums[i] with any integer from the range [nums[i] - k, nums[i] + k]. An array's beauty is the length of the longest subsequence consisting of equal elements. Return the maximum possible beauty of nums after applying the operation any number of times.

examples.explanation: We can choose nums[0] -> 3, nums[1] -> 4, nums[3] -> 4. Longest subsequence of identical elements is of length 3.

title: My Calendar I
description: You are implementing a program to use as your calendar. We can add a new event if adding the event will not cause a double booking (two events have some non-empty intersection). Implement the MyCalendar class: MyCalendar() initializes the calendar object, and book(int startTime, int endTime) returns true if the event can be added to the calendar successfully without causing a double booking.

examples.explanation: Event [10, 20] is booked. Event [15, 25] cannot be booked because it overlaps. Event [20, 30] can be booked.

constraints: At most 1000 calls will be made to book.

title: Diagonal Traverse II
description: Given a 2D integer array nums, return all elements of nums in diagonal order. Each diagonal traverses from bottom-left to top-right.

examples.explanation: Traverses ragged matrix along diagonals.

title: Sort Transformed Array
description: Given a sorted integer array nums and three integers a, b and c, apply a quadratic function of the form f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c to each element x in the array, and return the array in sorted order in O(n) time.

examples.explanation: Sorted transformed results.

constraints: nums is sorted in ascending order.

title: Hand of Straights
description: Alice has some number of cards and she wants to rearrange the cards into groups so that each group is of size groupSize, and consists of groupSize consecutive cards. Given an integer array hand where hand[i] is the value written on the ith card and an integer groupSize, return true if she can rearrange the cards, or false otherwise.

examples.explanation: Alice's hand can be rearranged as [1,2,3], [2,3,4], [6,7,8].
Alice's hand cannot be rearranged into groups of 4.

title: Product Price at a Given Date
description: Write a solution to find the prices of all products on the date '2019-08-16'. Assume the price of all products before any change is 10. Return the result table in any order.

examples.explanation: Extracts the latest price for each product on or before 2019-08-16, defaulting to 10 if no prior price changes occurred.

constraints: (product_id, change_date) is the primary key of the Products table.
Each row of this table indicates that the price of some product was changed to a new_price on change_date.

title: Implement Magic Dictionary
description: Design a data structure that is initialized with a list of different words. Provided a string, determine if you can change exactly one character in this string to match any string in the data structure. Implement the MagicDictionary class: MagicDictionary() initializes the object, buildDict(String[] dictionary) sets the dictionary of distinct strings, and search(String searchWord) returns true if you can change exactly one character in searchWord to match any string in the data structure.

examples.explanation: "hhllo" can be transformed into "hello" by modifying exactly one character 'h' to 'e'.

constraints: dictionary[i] consists of only lowercase English letters.
All the strings in dictionary are distinct.
searchWord consists of only lowercase English letters.
buildDict will be called only once.
At most 100 calls will be made to search.

title: Rabbits in Forest
description: There is a forest with an unknown number of rabbits. We asked n rabbits 'How many rabbits have a color similar to yours?' and recorded their answers in an integer array answers where answers[i] is the answer of the ith rabbit. Given the array answers, return the minimum number of rabbits that could be in the forest.

examples.explanation: The two rabbits that answered "1" could both be the same color, say red (2 rabbits). The rabbit that answered "2" must be a different color, say blue (3 rabbits). Total minimum rabbits = 2 + 3 = 5.
All three rabbits could be the same color, meaning there are 11 rabbits of that color in total.

title: Linked List Components
description: You are given the head of a linked list containing unique integer values and an integer array nums that is a subset of the linked list values. Return the number of connected components in nums, where two values are connected if they appear consecutively in the linked list.

examples.explanation: 0 and 1 are connected, so [0, 1] and [3] are the two connected components.
0 and 1 are connected, 3 and 4 are connected. Thus, [0, 1] and [3, 4] are the two connected components.

constraints: The number of nodes in the linked list is n.
All the values Node.val are unique.
All the values of nums are unique.

title: Binary Tree Vertical Order Traversal
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the vertical order traversal of its nodes' values. (i.e., from top to bottom, column by column). If two nodes are in the same row and column, the order should be from left to right.

examples.explanation: Column -1: [9], Column 0: [3, 15], Column 1: [20], Column 2: [7].
Nodes traversed vertical column by column.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 100].

title: Number of Boomerangs
description: You are given n points in the plane that are all distinct, where points[i] = [x_i, y_i]. A boomerang is a tuple of points (i, j, k) such that the distance between i and j equals the distance between i and k (the order of the tuple matters). Return the number of boomerangs.

examples.explanation: The two boomerangs centered at [2,2].
No boomerangs can be formed with fewer than 3 points.

title: Non-overlapping Intervals
description: Given an array of intervals intervals where intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i], return the minimum number of intervals you need to remove to make the rest of the intervals non-overlapping. Note that intervals which only touch at a point are non-overlapping. For example, [1, 2] and [2, 3] are non-overlapping.

examples.explanation: [1,3] can be removed and the rest of the intervals are non-overlapping.
You need to remove two [1,2] to make the rest of the intervals non-overlapping.

title: Number of Substrings With Only 1s
description: Given a binary string s, return the number of substrings with all characters 1's. Since the answer may be too large, return it modulo 10^9 + 7.

examples.explanation: There are 9 substrings in total with only 1's: "1" -> 5 times, "11" -> 3 times, "111" -> 1 time.
Substrings "1" appear twice.

title: Max Number of K-Sum Pairs
description: You are given an integer array nums and an integer k. In one operation, you can pick two numbers from the array whose sum equals k and remove them from the array. Return the maximum number of operations you can perform on the array.

examples.explanation: Starting with nums = [1,2,3,4]: Remove numbers 1 and 4, then remove numbers 2 and 3. A total of 2 operations.
Starting with nums = [3,1,3,4,3]: Remove the first two 3's, then nums = [1,4,3]. No more pairs sum to 6. Total of 1 operation.

title: Longest Substring with At Most Two Distinct Characters
description: Given a string s, return the length of the longest substring that contains at most two distinct characters.

examples.explanation: The substring is "ece" which its length is 3.
The substring is "aabbb" which its length is 5.

title: Find the Maximum Length of Valid Subsequence II
description: You are given an integer array nums and a positive integer k. A subsequence sub of nums with length x is called valid if (sub[0] + sub[1]) % k == (sub[1] + sub[2]) % k == ... == (sub[x - 2] + sub[x - 1]) % k. Return the length of the longest valid subsequence of nums.

examples.explanation: The longest valid subsequence is [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] where adjacent sums modulo 2 are all equal to 1.
The longest valid subsequence is [1, 4, 1, 4].

title: Paths in Maze That Lead to Same Room
description: A maze consists of n rooms numbered from 1 to n, and some corridors connecting them. You are given a 2D integer array corridors where corridors[i] = [room1_i, room2_i] indicates that there is a corridor connecting room1_i and room2_i. A cycle of length 3 (a triangle) is a set of three distinct rooms where each room is connected to the other two. Return the number of different cycles of length 3 in the maze.

examples.explanation: The cycles of length 3 are [1, 2, 4] and [1, 3, 4].
There are no cycles of length 3.

title: Ambiguous Coordinates
description: We had some 2-dimensional coordinates, like "(1, 3)" or "(2, 0.5)". Then we removed all commas, decimal points, and spaces, and ended up with the string s. Return a list of strings representing all possibilities for what our original coordinates could have been.

examples.explanation: All valid ways to place comma and decimal points.
Avoiding invalid leading/trailing zero coordinate strings.

constraints: The rest of s are digits.

title: 4 Keys Keyboard
description: Imagine you have a special keyboard with the following four keys: Key 1: (A): Print one 'A' on screen, Key 2: (Ctrl-A): Select the whole screen, Key 3: (Ctrl-C): Copy selection to buffer, Key 4: (Ctrl-V): Print buffer on screen appending it after what has already been printed. Given an integer n, return the maximum number of 'A' you can print on the screen with at most n keypresses.

examples.explanation: We can at most get 3 A's on screen by pressing following key sequence: A, A, A.
We can at most get 9 A's on screen by pressing: A, A, A, Ctrl-A, Ctrl-C, Ctrl-V, Ctrl-V.

title: Subarray Sums Divisible by K
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the number of non-empty subarrays that have a sum divisible by k. A subarray is a contiguous part of an array.

examples.explanation: No subarray has sum divisible by 9.

title: Minimum Domino Rotations For Equal Row
description: In a row of dominoes, tops[i] and bottoms[i] represent the top and bottom halves of the ith domino. In one move, we can rotate the ith domino so that tops[i] and bottoms[i] swap values. Return the minimum number of rotations so that all the values in tops are the same, or all the values in bottoms are the same. If it cannot be done, return -1.

examples.explanation: Rotate the second and fourth dominoes to make all tops equal to 2 (2 rotations).
In this case, it is not possible to rotate the dominoes to make one row of values equal.

title: Shortest Distance to Target Color
description: You are given an array colors, in which there are three colors: 1, 2 and 3. You are also given some queries. Each query consists of two integers i and c, return the shortest distance between the given index i and the target color c. If there is no direction towards the given color, return -1.

examples.explanation: The nearest 3 from index 1 is at index 4 (3 steps). Nearest 2 from index 2 is at index 2 (0 steps). Nearest 1 from index 6 is at index 3 (3 steps).

title: Restore IP Addresses
description: A valid IP address consists of exactly four integers separated by single dots. Each integer is between 0 and 255 (inclusive) and cannot have leading zeros. Given a string s containing only digits, return all possible valid IP addresses that can be formed by inserting dots into s.

examples.explanation: Both generated IP addresses are valid representations.
Only one valid IP address can be formed.

title: Car Pooling
description: There is a car with capacity empty seats. The vehicle only drives east. You are given the integer capacity and an array trips where trips[i] = [numPassengers_i, from_i, to_i] indicates that the ith trip has numPassengers_i passengers and the locations to pick up and drop them off are from_i and to_i respectively. Return true if it is possible to pick up and drop off all passengers for all the given trips, or false otherwise.

examples.explanation: At location 3, passengers from both trips are inside the car (total 5 passengers > capacity 4).
Car capacity is never exceeded.

title: Immediate Food Delivery II
description: If the customer's preferred delivery date is the same as the order date, then the order is called immediate; otherwise, it is called scheduled. The first order of a customer is the order with the earliest order date that the customer made. Write a solution to find the percentage of immediate orders in the first orders of all customers, rounded to 2 decimal places.

examples.explanation: Percentage of first orders where order_date equals customer_pref_delivery_date.

constraints: delivery_id is the primary key of the table.
The table holds information about food delivery orders.

title: Bulb Switcher
description: There are n bulbs that are initially off. You first turn on all the bulbs, then you turn off every second bulb. On the third round, you toggle every third bulb. For the ith round, you toggle every ith bulb. For the nth round, you only toggle the last bulb. Return the number of bulbs that are on after n rounds.

examples.explanation: Initial: [off, off, off]. Round 1: [on, on, on]. Round 2: [on, off, on]. Round 3: [on, off, off]. Only 1 bulb is on.
No bulbs are on.

title: House Robber III
description: The thief has found himself a new place for his thievery again. There is only one entrance to this area, called root. Besides the root, each house has one and only one parent house. After a tour, the smart thief realized that all houses in this place form a binary tree. It will automatically contact the police if two directly-linked houses were broken into on the same night. Return the maximum amount of money the thief can rob without alerting the police.

examples.explanation: Maximum amount of money the thief can rob = 3 + 3 + 1 = 7.
Maximum amount of money the thief can rob = 4 + 5 = 9.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 10^4].

title: Word Subsets
description: You are given two string arrays words1 and words2. A string b is a subset of string a if every letter in b occurs in a including multiplicity. A string a from words1 is universal if for every string b in words2, b is a subset of a. Return an array of all the universal strings in words1.

examples.explanation: All three strings contain at least one 'e' and one 'o'.
Universal words contain both 'l' and 'e'.

constraints: words1[i] and words2[i] consist only of lowercase English letters.
All words in words1 are unique.

title: Count Numbers with Unique Digits
description: Given an integer n, return the count of all numbers with unique digits, x, where 0 <= x < 10^n.

examples.explanation: The answer should be the total numbers in the range of 0 <= x < 100, excluding 11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 77, 88, 99.
Only x = 0 has unique digits.

title: Campus Bikes II
description: On a campus represented by a 2D grid, there are n workers and m bikes, with n <= m. Each worker and bike is a 2D coordinate. We assign one unique bike to each worker so that the sum of the Manhattan distances between each worker and their assigned bike is minimized. Return the minimum possible sum of Manhattan distances between each worker and their assigned bike.

examples.explanation: Worker 0 gets Bike 0, Worker 1 gets Bike 1. Distance = |0-1| + |0-2| + |2-3| + |1-3| = 3 + 3 = 6.
Optimal assignment minimizes total Manhattan distance to 2.

title: Magical String
description: A magical string s consists only of '1' and '2' and obeys the rule that concatenating the number of contiguous occurrences of characters produces the string s itself. Given an integer n, return the number of '1's in the first n number in the magical string s.

examples.explanation: The first 6 elements of magical string s is "122112" and it contains three 1s, so return 3.
The first element is "1", which contains one 1.

title: Prime Subtraction Operation
description: You are given a 0-indexed integer array nums of length n. You can pick a prime p strictly less than nums[i] and subtract p from nums[i] at most once for each index i. Return true if you can make nums a strictly increasing array using the above operation on numbers in nums.

examples.explanation: Subtract 3 from nums[0] (1), subtract 7 from nums[1] (2), subtract 3 from nums[2] (3), subtract 5 from nums[3] (5). Resulting array [1, 2, 3, 5] is strictly increasing.
Already strictly increasing without needing changes.

title: Find a Peak Element II
description: A peak element in a 2D grid is an element that is strictly greater than all of its adjacent neighbors to the left, right, top, and bottom. Given a 0-indexed m x n matrix mat where no two adjacent cells are equal, find any peak element mat[i][j] and return the length 2 array [i, j]. You must write an algorithm that runs in O(m log(n)) or O(n log(m)) time.

examples.explanation: Both 3 and 4 are peak elements. [0, 1] points to element 4.
30 is strictly greater than 20, 21, 14, and 16.

constraints: No two adjacent cells are equal.

title: The Maze II
description: There is a ball in a maze with empty spaces (0) and walls (1). The ball can go through empty spaces by rolling up, down, left or right, but it won't stop rolling until hitting a wall. Find the shortest distance for the ball to stop at the destination. The distance is defined by the number of empty spaces traveled by the ball from the start position to the destination. Return the shortest distance, or -1 if the ball cannot stop at the destination.

examples.explanation: One shortest way is : left -> down -> left -> down -> right -> down -> right with distance 12.
The ball cannot stop at the destination.

title: Largest Sum of Averages
description: You are given an integer array nums and an integer k. You can partition the array into at most k non-empty adjacent subarrays. The score of a partition is the sum of the averages of each subarray. Return the maximum score you can achieve of all the possible partitions.

examples.explanation: Partitioning nums into [9], [1, 2, 3], [9] gives score 9 + (1 + 2 + 3) / 3 + 9 = 20.
Optimal partition produces maximal average score 20.5.

title: Magic Squares In Grid
description: A 3 x 3 magic square is a 3 x 3 grid filled with distinct numbers from 1 to 9 such that each row, column, and both diagonals all have the same sum. Given a row x col grid of integers, how many 3 x 3 contiguous magic square subgrids are there?

examples.explanation: The subgrid [[4,3,8],[9,5,1],[2,7,6]] is a magic square.
No 3x3 subgrid exists.

title: Longest Uploaded Prefix
description: You are given a stream of n videos, each represented by a distinct number from 1 to n. Implement the LUPrefix class: LUPrefix(int n) initializes the object for a stream of n videos, upload(int video) uploads a video with the given number, and longest() returns the length of the longest uploaded prefix.

examples.explanation: After uploading 3, prefix is 0. After uploading 1, prefix is 1. After uploading 2, prefix is 3 (1, 2, 3 uploaded).

constraints: All values of video are distinct.
At most 2 * 10^5 calls in total will be made to upload and longest.

title: Delete Node in a BST
description: Given a root node reference of a BST and a key, delete the node with the given key in the BST. Return the root node reference (possibly updated) of the BST.

examples.explanation: Given key to delete is 3. One valid answer is [5,4,6,2,null,null,7].
Key does not exist in BST, so no change.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 10^4].
Each node has a unique value.
root is a valid binary search tree.

title: Design Circular Queue
description: Design your implementation of the circular queue. The circular queue is a linear data structure in which the operations are performed based on FIFO (First In First Out) principle, and the last position is connected back to the first position to make a circle. Implement the MyCircularQueue class with enQueue, deQueue, Front, Rear, isEmpty, and isFull methods.

examples.output: [null, true, true, true, false, 3, true, true, true, 4]
examples.explanation: Circular queue correctly maintains FIFO buffer within fixed capacity of 3.

constraints: At most 3000 calls will be made to enQueue, deQueue, Front, Rear, isEmpty, and isFull.

title: Find the Maximum Length of Valid Subsequence I
description: You are given an integer array nums. A subsequence sub of nums with length x is called valid if (sub[0] + sub[1]) % 2 == (sub[1] + sub[2]) % 2 == ... == (sub[x - 2] + sub[x - 1]) % 2. Return the length of the longest valid subsequence of nums.

examples.explanation: The longest valid subsequence is [1, 2, 3, 4] where all adjacent parity sums equal 1 (odd).
The longest valid subsequence is [1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2].

title: Binary Tree Longest Consecutive Sequence
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the length of the longest consecutive sequence path. The path refers to any sequence of nodes from some starting node to any node, through the parent-child relationships. The longest consecutive path need to be from parent to child (cannot be the reverse).

examples.explanation: Longest consecutive sequence path is 3-4-5, so return 3.
Longest consecutive sequence path is 2-3, not 3-2-1, so return 2.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 3 * 10^4].

title: Subarray Product Less Than K
description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, return the number of contiguous subarrays where the product of all the elements in the subarray is strictly less than k.

examples.explanation: The 8 subarrays that have product less than 100 are: [10], [5], [2], [6], [10, 5], [5, 2], [2, 6], [5, 2, 6].
No subarray has product less than 0.

title: Path With Maximum Minimum Value
description: Given an m x n integer matrix grid, return the maximum score of a path starting at (0, 0) and ending at (m - 1, n - 1) moving in the 4 cardinal directions. The score of a path is the minimum value in that path.

examples.explanation: The path with the maximum score is 5 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 6 with score 4.
All nodes along the optimal path have values >= 2.

title: Zero Array Transformation III
description: You are given an integer array nums and a 2D integer array queries. Each query allows choosing a subsegment to decrement. Find the maximum number of queries that can be removed from queries such that nums can still be transformed to all zeros using the remaining queries, or return -1 if it is impossible.

examples.explanation: Removing query [1,1] allows the two [0,2] queries to decrement nums[0] and nums[2] to 0.

title: Longest Arithmetic Subsequence of Given Difference
description: Given an integer array arr and an integer difference, return the length of the longest subsequence in arr which is an arithmetic sequence such that the difference between adjacent elements in the subsequence equals difference.

examples.explanation: The longest arithmetic subsequence is [1,2,3,4].
No two adjacent elements have difference 1, longest is length 1.
The longest arithmetic subsequence is [7,5,3,1].

title: Smallest Integer Divisible by K
description: Given a positive integer k, you need to find the length of the smallest positive integer n such that n is divisible by k, and n only contains the digit 1. Return the length of n. If there is no such n, return -1.

examples.explanation: The smallest answer is n = 1, which has length 1.
There is no such integer divisible by 2.
The smallest answer is n = 111, which has length 3.

title: Count Number of Bad Pairs
description: You are given a 0-indexed integer array nums. A pair of indices (i, j) is a bad pair if i < j and j - i != nums[j] - nums[i]. Return the total number of bad pairs in nums.

examples.explanation: There are no bad pairs.
